definition_zh: 有创造力的；创作性的；新颖的
definition_en: good at making new and interesting things; using imagination
core_image: 脑袋里不断冒出新点子的人
scene: 手抄报比赛前，同桌用旧邮票和树叶拼出了一幅小花园。 My deskmate is very creative and full of ideas.
sceneCN: 这里 creative 是「有创造力的」（第 1 个义项：善于想出新点子）；句意是我的同桌非常有创造力，点子层出不穷。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「创造；创作」
由 creative 加 -ity 构成，义为「创造力」
由 create 加 -ion 构成，义为「作品；创造物」
由 creative 加副词后缀构成，义为「有创意地」

senses.title: Good at thinking of new ideas
senses.definition: able to think of new, interesting ideas or ways of doing things
senses.definitionCN: 能想出新奇有趣的点子或做法
senses.example: Creative pupils solved the puzzle in three different ways.
senses.exampleCN: 有创造力的学生用三种不同方法解出了这道谜题。
senses.why: The core image is a maker's mind, so anyone who keeps producing fresh ideas is creative.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是造物者的头脑，所以不断产出新点子的人就是 creative。

senses.title: Connected with art and imagination
senses.definition: involving art, stories, music or design that uses imagination
senses.definitionCN: 涉及需要想象力的艺术、故事、音乐或设计
senses.example: Creative writing class meets every Friday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 创意写作课每周五下午上课。
senses.why: Since art is the clearest place for making new things, the word labels art classes and artists.
senses.whyCN: 因为艺术是造新事物最明显的领域，所以这个词也用来标记艺术课和艺术家。

senses.title: Using things in surprising new ways
senses.titleCN: 把普通东西用出新花样
senses.definition: using ordinary things or time in clever, unexpected ways
senses.definitionCN: 巧妙而出人意料地使用普通物品或时间
senses.example: She was creative with old bottles, turning them into pencil holders.
senses.exampleCN: 她把旧瓶子用出了新意，做成笔筒。
senses.why: A new idea does not need new material; old things rearranged show the same maker's mind.
senses.whyCN: 新点子不需要新材料，把旧物重新组合同样体现造物者的头脑。

intro.en: Creative is a young adjective built on the old Latin root of create.
intro.cn: creative 是建立在 create 古老拉丁词根上的较年轻的形容词。

items.en: The root creare meant to make or bring forth.
items.cn: 词根 creare 意为造出、使产生。

items.en: The suffix -ivus made adjectives meaning able or given to doing.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成形容词，表示「有做某事的倾向」。

items.en: English verbs like create settled in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: create 等英语动词在十四世纪固定下来。

items.en: The adjective creative appeared in the eighteenth century as art and invention grew.
items.cn: 十八世纪随着艺术与发明的发展，形容词 creative 出现了。

items.en: Today creative names people, classes and industries built on imagination.
items.cn: 如今 creative 指人、课程和以想象力为基础的行业。

note.en: These words share the create root or name inventive minds.
note.cn: 这些词与 create 同根，或指善于发明创造的头脑。

normalIntro.en: Build the word openly: create + ive.
normalIntro.cn: 把构词摊开看：create + ive。

normal.en: create + -ive = creative, full of create power.
normal.cn: create + -ive ＝ creative，充满创造能力。

normal.en: creativity swaps -ive for -ivity as the noun.
normal.cn: 名词把 -ive 换成 -ivity：creativity。

normal.en: creatively is the adverb for how artists work.
normal.cn: creatively 是副词，说明艺术家的工作方式。

normal.en: Creative writing is a real school subject name.
normal.cn: creative writing 是真实的课程名。

normal.en: Original means not copied, a close meaning partner.
normal.cn: original 意为不抄袭，是近义伙伴。

abstract.en: See a lightbulb flick on over a doodling head.
abstract.cn: 看一个涂鸦的脑袋上方亮起灯泡。

abstract.en: Watch old jars become lanterns on a birthday night.
abstract.cn: 看旧罐子在生日夜变成灯笼。

abstract.en: Feel the fun of one question with five right answers.
abstract.cn: 感受一道题有五种正确答案的乐趣。

examples.en: Our creative writing group wrote a play together.
examples.cn: 我们的创意写作小组一起写了一个剧本。

examples.en: Being creative helps you solve problems faster.
examples.cn: 有创造力能帮你更快解决问题。

examples.en: The most creative entry won first prize.
examples.cn: 最有创意的作品获得了一等奖。

sensesIntro.en: From idea machines, to art classes, to clever reuse of old things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从点子机器，到艺术课堂，再到旧物的巧妙新用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a head that keeps making new things
core.cn: 核心意象：不断造出新东西的头脑

branches.en: Many fresh solutions to one puzzle
branches.cn: 一道谜题的多种新解法

branches.en: Writing, music and art lessons
branches.cn: 写作、音乐与美术课

branches.en: Old bottles turned into holders
branches.cn: 旧瓶子变身笔筒

branches.en: New ideas from old materials
branches.cn: 旧材料生出新点子

branches.en: The art flag on the word
branches.cn: 这个词的艺术标签

intro.cn: creative 展示了拉丁动词披上形容词后缀的样子。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 creare 意为造出、使产生。

definition_zh: 使用；利用；消耗；用掉；对待
definition_en: to do something with a tool or thing for a purpose, or to take and consume something
core_image: 伸手把工具从抽屉里拿出来握在手中
scene: 厨房的抽屉一拉开，里面躺着各式各样的工具，母亲总能顺手拿出合适的那个。 A good cook knows how to use every pot in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 use 是「使用、利用」（第 1 个义项：拿工具去做事）；句意为好厨师懂得使用厨房里的每一口锅。伸手取工具的这幅画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成，义为「用户；使用者」
加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「用法；使用量」
加 -ful 构成，义为「有用的」
加 -less 构成，义为「无用的」
加 -able 构成，义为「可用的」

senses.title: To employ a thing for a purpose
senses.definition: to do something with a tool, object, or method in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个结果而用工具、物品或方法去做事
senses.example: She used a sharp knife to cut the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一把快刀切面包。
senses.why: The verb names the act of taking something into one's hands and making it serve a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就指「把东西拿到手里，让它为自己办事」，取用工具的意象就是它的本义。

senses.title: To spend or consume a supply
senses.definition: to consume an amount of something such as time, money, or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 消耗掉一定量的时间、金钱或燃料等
senses.example: The old truck uses a lot of fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧卡车很费油。
senses.why: Whatever is put to work is partly spent in the process, so the same verb comes to mean using up a supply.
senses.whyCN: 东西一旦被动用来干活，过程中总要耗掉一部分，于是同一个动词就引申为「耗用」。

senses.title: The act or purpose of employing something
senses.definition: as a noun, the act of employing something or the purpose it serves
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指使用的行为，或某物所起的作用
senses.example: This room is for the use of guests only.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间仅供客人使用。
senses.why: The nouns formed from the verb simply name the action itself and the end it serves.
senses.whyCN: 由这个动词转成的名词只是把「使用」这个动作本身和它所服务的目的命名下来。

senses.title: To treat someone in a particular way
senses.definition: to behave towards somebody in a stated manner, often unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式对待某人，常含有不公平的意味
senses.example: He felt that his boss had used him badly.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得老板待他很刻薄。
senses.why: To use people is to treat them as tools; from that picture the verb widens into simply meaning to treat.
senses.whyCN: 把人当工具使，就是把对方当成器物；从这个画面出发，词义又扩大到泛指的「对待」。

senses.title: To take a drug or apply a substance
senses.definition: to take a drug, medicine, or other substance regularly or deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地、经常地服用药物或使用某种物质
senses.example: The doctor told him to use the cream twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 医生让他每天涂两次这种药膏。
senses.why: Medicine is a supply applied to the body for a result, so it slips naturally into the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 药物就是施用于身体、换取疗效的东西，于是它自然套进了同一个句法框架。

intro.en: A short word from Old French, ultimately from Latin, that has kept its shape almost unchanged for eight centuries.
intro.cn: 一个来自古法语、最终可溯至拉丁语的小词，八百年来词形几乎没有变化。

items.en: Usus, the past participle of uti, meant a using or a practice, and usare was a frequentative form of the same verb.
items.cn: usus 是 uti 的过去分词，意为「使用、惯行」；usare 是同一动词的反复体形式。

items.en: Us, user, and the past participle usé carried the verb into everyday French for using and wearing out.
items.cn: us、user 以及过去分词 usé 把这个动词带进日常法语，兼表「使用」与「用旧」。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the thirteenth century as usen, with the noun use beside it.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪以 usen 的形式借入这个动词，名词 use 并行存在。

items.en: Spelling settles on use, and the word already covers tools, supplies, and medicine.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 use，词义这时已覆盖工具、物资与药物。

items.en: The question what is this used for turns the verb and noun into the commonest way of asking about purpose.
items.cn: what is this used for 这类问句让动词和名词成为询问用途最常用的手段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the close relatives of the verb, while the near-meaning group sets tools against overuse and waste.
note.cn: 形近组收集这个动词的近亲，近义组则把使用与误用、滥用、浪费放在一起对照。

normalIntro.en: Three letters that name the everyday act of taking a thing and making it work for you.
normalIntro.cn: 三个字母，命名的是日常里把东西拿来替你办事的动作。

normal.en: Use up means finish the supply, as in use up all the paper.
normal.cn: use up 表示把存货用尽，如 use up all the paper。

normal.en: Make use of is the fixed phrase for turning something to your advantage.
normal.cn: make use of 是「加以利用」的固定说法。

normal.en: In use describes a machine that is working at this moment.
normal.cn: in use 形容机器此刻正在使用中。

normal.en: The noun use is pronounced with a soft s, the verb with a hard z.
normal.cn: 名词 use 末尾读清音 s，动词则读浊音 z。

normal.en: User, usage, useful, and useless all sit on this same short base.
normal.cn: user、usage、useful、useless 都建立在这个短词干上。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer of knives and spoons, and a hand closing on exactly the right one.
abstract.cn: 想象一抽屉的刀叉勺子，一只手正好抓住了对的那一件。

abstract.en: Feel the grip of a handle that many other hands have worn smooth.
abstract.cn: 体会一只被许多只手磨得光滑的把手。

abstract.en: Watch a full jar of coffee slowly empty day after day.
abstract.cn: 看着满满一罐咖啡一天天空下去。

examples.en: She used an old spoon to dig a hole for the seeds.
examples.cn: 她用一把旧勺子挖了个坑埋种子。

examples.en: We used up all the firewood before the snow came.
examples.cn: 雪落下之前我们把木柴都用光了。

examples.en: Learning to use a map is still a useful skill on long hikes.
examples.cn: 学会用地图在长途徒步中仍是一项有用的技能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优使」——把最好用的工具交给能干的人去使用。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）及其过去分词 usus、反复体 usare，经古法语 us / user 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One act of taking a thing into service spreads to spending supplies, to the act itself, to treating people, and to taking medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把东西拿来用」这一个动作出发，词义扩展到耗用物资、使用行为、对待他人以及服用药物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taking a tool and putting it to work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手取出工具，让它开始干活。

branches.en: The tool branch: a thing made to serve a purpose.
branches.cn: 工具分支：让某物为某个目的服务。

branches.en: The supply branch: use eats into a store of fuel, money, or time.
branches.cn: 物资分支：使用会吃掉油、钱、时间的存量。

branches.en: The noun branch: the act itself and the purpose it serves.
branches.cn: 名词分支：使用这一行为以及它服务的目的。

branches.en: The people branch: treating someone as a tool.
branches.cn: 人事分支：把某人当作工具来对待。

branches.en: The medicine branch: a substance applied for a result.
branches.cn: 药物分支：为求疗效而施用的物质。

intro.en: The word is barely analysable today, but two Latin pieces are still readable behind it.
intro.cn: 这个词如今几乎无法拆分，但其背后仍能读出两个拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb uti, to use, gives usus and the frequentative usare; the short stem is all that survives in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 uti（使用）给出 usus 与反复体 usare，英语只留下了这条短词干。

items.example: The stem us- carries the whole idea of using.
items.exampleCN: 词干 us- 承载了「使用」的全部含义。

items.example: Use as a verb keeps a silent final e.
items.exampleCN: 作动词的 use 末尾有一个不发音的 e。

items.example: Use gives user, a person who uses.
items.exampleCN: use 加它成为 user，即使用者。

items.example: Usage means the way or amount of use.
items.exampleCN: usage 表示用法或使用量。

items.example: Usable means able to be used.
Misuse is the wrong kind of use.

definition_zh: 海豹；印章；封口；密封
definition_en: a sea animal with flippers, a stamped mark, a closed fastening, or to close something tightly
core_image: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳，胡须上还挂着水珠
scene: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。 A seal lay on the ice in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 seal 是「海豹」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。

derivatives.zh: 密封剂
密封的
密封剂；封口者
开封

senses.title: A sea animal
senses.definition: a sea animal with flippers that rests on land or ice
senses.definitionCN: 有鳍状肢、在陆地或冰上休息的海洋动物
senses.example: A seal swam beside the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 一只海豹在船边游动。
senses.why: One word comes from an old name for this animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的一个来源就是这种动物的古称。

senses.title: A stamped mark
senses.definition: a device or mark pressed onto a document to prove it is genuine
senses.definitionCN: 盖在文件上以证明其真实的器具或印记
senses.example: The letter bore the king's seal.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信上有国王的印章。
senses.why: A pressed mark closes and certifies a document.
senses.whyCN: 压印的标记封闭并证明文件。

senses.title: A closed fastening
senses.definition: something that closes an opening tightly
senses.definitionCN: 把开口紧密封闭的东西
senses.example: The seal on the jar was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子上的封口被打开了。
senses.why: The certified mark becomes a physical closure.
senses.whyCN: 认证标记变成物理封口。

senses.title: To close tightly
senses.definition: to close something so that air or liquid cannot pass
senses.definitionCN: 封闭某物使空气或液体无法通过
senses.example: She sealed the envelope with wax.
senses.exampleCN: 她用蜡把信封封好。
senses.why: The noun of closure becomes the action of closing.
senses.whyCN: 封闭物的名词义转为封闭动作。

intro.en: Seal is two words in one: Old English seolh, the animal, and Latin sigillum, a small stamp.
intro.cn: seal 是两个词合流：古英语 seolh（海豹）与拉丁语 sigillum（小图章）。

items.en: Seolh named the sea animal.
items.cn: seolh 指海豹这种海洋动物。

items.en: Sigillum meant a small picture or stamp.
items.cn: sigillum 意为小图像或印章。

items.en: Seel meant a stamp used on documents.
items.cn: seel 指用于文件的印章。

items.en: Seal named both the animal and the stamp.
items.cn: seal 同时指海豹与印章。

items.en: Seal also meant to close a document formally.
items.cn: seal 也开始表示正式封住文件。

items.en: Seal means to close tightly or to block an area.
items.cn: 现代英语中 seal 意为密封或封锁区域。

note.en: Seal is compared with similar short words and with words for stamps and closures.
note.cn: 把 seal 与形近短词以及表示印章和封闭的词作比较。

abstract.en: A stamp that proves a document also closes it.

sensesIntro.en: Seal means a sea animal, a stamped mark, a closure, or to close something tightly.
sensesIntro.cn: seal 意为海豹、印章、封口，或密封。

core.en: A mark or closure that makes something secure.
core.cn: 使某物安全可靠的印记或封闭。

branches.en: The animal of cold seas.
branches.cn: 寒冷海域的动物。

branches.en: A mark that proves a document.
branches.cn: 证明文件的印记。

branches.en: A physical closure on a container.
branches.cn: 容器上的物理封口。

branches.en: The action of closing tightly.
branches.cn: 紧密封闭的动作。

branches.en: Stamping and sealing both finish a document.
branches.cn: 盖章与密封都完成文件处理。

intro.en: Seal forms words for closing materials and actions.
intro.cn: seal 构成表示密封材料与动作的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin sigillum is the source of the stamp sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sigillum 是印章义的来源。

items.meaning: an animal, a stamp, or to close

items.example: Sealing the jar keeps food fresh.
items.exampleCN: 密封罐子能让食物保鲜。

items.meaning: a substance or person that seals

items.exampleCN: 法院公开了密封的记录。

items.example: He wore a silver seal ring.
items.exampleCN: 他戴着一枚银印章戒指。

definition_zh: 使着迷；迷住；使心醉神迷
definition_en: to hold someone's attention completely, as if under a spell
core_image: 篝火在黑暗中跳动，围观者的眼睛映着火光，谁也挪不动脚步
scene: 自然课上老师放了一段深海录像，发光的水母缓缓漂过屏幕。 The glowing jellyfish fascinated the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里指「使着迷」，对应第 1 个义项：强烈吸引使其无法移开目光；句意为发光的水母把全班迷住了。画面要点：暗教室、屏幕蓝光、发光水母。

pos.zh: 使着迷；迷住；使神魂颠倒

derivatives.zh: 迷人的（现在分词作形容词）
着迷的（过去分词作形容词）
魅力；着迷（名词化）
迷人之物；羽饰头帽（罕用）
未被迷住的（否定分词，罕用）

senses.title: To hold attention completely
senses.definition: to interest someone so strongly that they cannot look away
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地吸引某人，使其无法移开目光
senses.example: The snake fascinated the bird.
senses.exampleCN: 蛇把鸟迷住了。
senses.why: The spell holds the eyes; fascination is attention that cannot escape.
senses.whyCN: 咒语锁住目光；着迷是无法逃脱的注意。

senses.title: To charm or enchant
senses.definition: to fill with delight and wonder
senses.definitionCN: 以愉悦与惊奇充满内心
senses.example: She was fascinated by the northern lights.
senses.exampleCN: 她被北极光迷住了。
senses.why: The old magic survives as wonder: enchantment without the witch.
senses.whyCN: 古老的魔法以惊奇存留：没有巫师的迷醉。

senses.title: To capture as if by a spell
senses.definition: to render unable to move or think clearly, as if under a spell
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛中了咒般无法动弹或清晰思考
senses.example: The crowd stood fascinated, unable to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 人群着了迷般站着，无法离开。
senses.why: The literal spell sense shows itself when willpower disappears.
senses.whyCN: 当意志力消失时，字面意义的咒术义便现身。

intro.en: Fascinate goes back to Latin fascinare, 'to cast a spell on', from fascinum, the evil spell or the charm against it.
intro.cn: fascinate 回溯拉丁语 fascinare「施咒」，出自 fascinum，即邪咒（或避邪的护符）。

items.en: Latin fascinum meant a spell or witchcraft; fascinare meant to enchant.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fascinum 指咒术；fascinare 意为施魔法迷住。

items.en: Late Latin fascinatus named one who has been enchanted.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 fascinatus 指被施了魔法之人。

items.en: Old French fasciner kept the sense of bewitching.
items.cn: 古法语 fasciner 保留「迷惑」之义。

items.en: Middle English fascinate meant to bewitch or cast a spell on someone.
items.cn: 中古英语 fascinate 意为对某人施咒。

items.en: Modern English weakened the magic into pure attraction: fascinated by a story, an idea, a face.
items.cn: 现代英语把魔法弱化为纯粹的吸引：被故事、想法或面孔迷住。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fasc- root (spell, bewitch); near-meaning words name degrees of captured attention.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fasc- 词根（施咒、迷住）；近义组命名注意力被俘获的不同程度。

entries.definitionCN: 动词的形容词形式：迷人的

entries.definition: causing death
entries.definitionCN: 致命的；拼写相近但源自拉丁 fatum

entries.definition: extraordinarily good
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；词根为希腊 phant-，不同源

entries.definition: to charm and hold attention
entries.definitionCN: 使迷住；语义平行，同指俘获注意

entries.definition: to delight as if by magic
to hold in a trance-like way

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for casting spells.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「施咒」之词，五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin fascinare meant to cast a spell; fascinate still casts one on your eyes.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fascinare＝施咒；fascinate 至今仍在你的眼睛上施咒。

normal.en: be fascinated by is the everyday pattern: fascinated by stars, by history.
normal.cn: be fascinated by 是日常句型：被星星、历史迷住。

normal.en: captivate and fascinate are twins: both seize your attention.
normal.cn: captivate 与 fascinate 是双胞胎：都俘获注意力。

normal.en: a fascinating book keeps you up too late.
normal.cn: a fascinating book 让你熬夜。

normal.en: fascination is the noun: a lifelong fascination with trains.
normal.cn: fascination 是名词：对火车一生一世的痴迷。

abstract.en: A spell is attention that has forgotten how to leave.
abstract.cn: 咒语是忘了如何离开的注意力。

abstract.en: Fascination is gravity for the eyes.
abstract.cn: 着迷是眼睛的引力。

abstract.en: Wonder is magic that gave up its wand and stayed.
abstract.cn: 惊奇是交出魔杖却不肯离场的魔法。

examples.en: The old map fascinated everyone in the museum.
examples.cn: 那张古地图让博物馆里的每个人都着了迷。

examples.en: He was fascinated by the way ants build their cities.
examples.cn: 蚂蚁筑巢的方式让他着迷。

examples.en: Her fascinating lecture made the hours disappear.
examples.cn: 她引人入胜的讲座让几个小时悄然流逝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法斯内特」——法术迅速内摄心神（fast in-net），一下把你网住 → 使着迷。

root: 拉丁语 fascinare（施咒迷住），出自 fascinum（咒术；护符）。经后期拉丁语与古法语 fasciner 进入英语，本义为施魔法，现代英语弱化为纯粹的强烈吸引。

sensesIntro.en: From casting spells outward to charm, wonder, and attention that cannot escape.
sensesIntro.cn: 从施咒扩展到迷醉、惊奇与无法逃脱的注意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes caught by firelight, too deep in to look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光被火光俘获，深陷其中无法移开。

branches.en: THE GAZE HELD: attention that cannot leave.
branches.cn: 被锁的目光：无法离开的注意。

branches.en: THE DELIGHT: enchantment softened into joy.
branches.cn: 迷醉：魔法软化为喜悦。

branches.en: THE SPELL: the literal magic of immobility.
branches.cn: 咒语：无法动弹的字面魔法。

branches.en: THE CHARM: attraction and wonder in one word.
branches.cn: 魅力：吸引与惊奇集于一词。

branches.en: THE CAPTURE: the mind taken whole.
branches.cn: 俘获：整颗心被拿住。

intro.en: Fascinate is the fasc- spell root in a verb suit; the family keeps its magical flavor.
intro.cn: fascinate 是 fasc- 咒术词根穿上动词外衣；词族保留魔法气息。

latinIntro.en: Latin fascinum and fascinare seed the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fascinum 与 fascinare 孕育词族。

items.meaning: to charm as if by magic

definition_zh: 图表；海图；航行图；排行榜；绘制图表
definition_en: a sheet giving facts in the form of pictures, lines or tables; a map for sailors; to make a chart of
core_image: 一张纸上用线条和图形把数字讲清楚，或一张领航的地图
scene: 科学课上，小组把一周的气温记录画成了折线图贴在墙上。 Our group drew a weather chart for the science class.
sceneCN: 这里 chart 是「图表」（第 1 个义项：把信息画成图形的纸）；句意为我们小组为科学课画了一张天气图表。

derivatives.zh: 由 chart 加 -ist 构成，历史上指靠图表研究行情的人
由 chart 加后缀构成，义为「无图表的；无海图的」

senses.title: A sheet showing facts as pictures or lines
senses.definition: a sheet of paper giving information in the form of pictures, lines or tables
senses.definitionCN: 用图形、线条或表格呈现信息的纸面
senses.example: Our group drew a weather chart for the science class.
senses.exampleCN: 我们小组为科学课画了一张天气图。
senses.why: A card was once any sheet of writing; when numbers are drawn instead of written, the sheet keeps the card's name.
senses.whyCN: card 本指写有文字的纸；当数字被画成图形，这张纸沿用了卡片的称呼。

senses.title: A map for sea or air travel
senses.definition: a map showing coasts, depths and dangers, used by sailors or pilots
senses.definitionCN: 标出海岸、水深与危险区域、供海员或飞行员使用的地图
senses.example: The captain studied the chart before leaving the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船长出港前仔细研究海图。
senses.why: A sailing map is just a special sheet of drawn information, so it borrows the same name.
senses.whyCN: 航海地图就是一张特殊的「画出来的信息纸」，于是借用了同一个名字。

senses.title: A weekly list of the most popular songs
senses.definition: a published list showing the most popular songs or records each week
senses.definitionCN: 每周公布的流行歌曲或唱片的排名表
senses.example: Their new song jumped to the top of the charts.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的新歌蹿升到排行榜第一。
senses.why: A ranking list is again information drawn on a sheet, extending the drawn-sheet idea to popularity.
senses.whyCN: 排名表同样是「画在纸上的信息」，把图形纸的概念延伸到流行度上。

senses.title: To make a chart or plan something
senses.definition: to draw a chart of something, or to plan a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 为某物绘制图表，或规划行动路线
senses.example: The nurse charted the patient's temperature every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每小时把病人体温记录成表。
senses.why: Making the drawn sheet becomes an action verb, like turning any tool's name into using it.
senses.whyCN: 绘制图形纸的动作化为动词，正如工具名常转为使用它的动作。

intro.en: Chart and card share one Latin word for a sheet of papyrus, splitting into two English forms.
intro.cn: chart 与 card 同出一个拉丁语「莎草纸」词，在英语里分成两种形式。

items.en: Latin charta meant a leaf of papyrus or paper for writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 charta 指可供书写的莎草纸或纸张。

items.en: It came from Greek chartes, a sheet made from papyrus reeds.
items.cn: 该词源自希腊语 chartes，指用莎草制成的纸页。

items.en: Old French charte meant a document or map, especially one with authority.
items.cn: 古法语 charte 指文件或地图，尤指有权威性的文书。

items.en: Middle English took chart for a map, especially a sea map.
items.cn: 中古英语用 chart 指地图，尤指海图。

items.en: Modern English keeps the drawn-sheet senses: diagrams, sea maps and hit lists.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了图形纸的各义：图表、海图与排行榜。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects information-display words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收信息呈现类词。

entries.definition: A vehicle with wheels for carrying goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手推车」，拼写与 chart 相近。

entries.definition: A vegetable with large leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甜菜叶」，拼写与 chart 相近。

entries.definition: An official document granting rights.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宪章；特许状」，与 chart 同源。

entries.definition: A drawing showing how numbers change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「曲线图」，与 chart 的图表义相近。

entries.definition: Facts arranged in rows and columns.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「表格」，同为信息呈现方式。

entries.definition: A drawing of roads, land or sea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地图」，与 chart 的海图义相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember chart by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chart。

normal.en: chart comes from Latin charta, a sheet of paper.
normal.cn: chart 源自拉丁语 charta（纸张）。

normal.en: card is its twin word from the same root.
normal.cn: card 是同根的孪生词。

normal.en: charter also shares the document root.
normal.cn: charter（宪章）同属「文书」词族。

normal.en: a pie chart looks like a cut pie.
normal.cn: pie chart（饼状图）像一块切开的饼。

normal.en: top the charts means to be number one in music.
normal.cn: top the charts 意为登顶音乐榜。

abstract.en: Picture bars of different heights marching across a grid.
abstract.cn: 想象高矮不一的柱子列队走过方格纸。

abstract.en: Hear the captain's pen tracing coastlines on a map.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见船长的笔在海图上描画海岸线。

abstract.en: Feel a song climbing one step at a time to number one.
abstract.cn: 感受一首歌一步步爬上榜首的位置。

examples.en: Our group drew a weather chart for the science class.
examples.cn: 我们小组为科学课画了一张天气图表。

examples.en: Their new song reached the top of the charts.
examples.cn: 他们的新歌登上了排行榜榜首。

examples.en: The nurse charted the patient's temperature every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时记录病人的体温。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「查特」——查一查特制的图表，数据一目了然。

root: 希腊语 chartes（莎草纸）→ 拉丁语 charta（纸张、文书）→ 古法语 charte → 中古英语 chart → 现代英语 chart；同根词有 card（卡片）、charter（宪章）。

sensesIntro.en: Chart moves from a written sheet to drawn data, sea maps, hit lists and the act of plotting.
sensesIntro.cn: chart 由书写纸延伸到图形数据、海图、排行榜与绘制动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: information drawn on a sheet
core.cn: 核心意象：画在纸面上的信息

branches.en: Facts shown as pictures
branches.cn: 画成图形的数据

branches.en: A map for sailing
branches.cn: 供航海使用的地图

branches.en: A popularity ranking list
branches.cn: 流行度排名表

branches.en: The act of recording data
branches.cn: 记录数据的动作

branches.en: Classroom data displays
branches.cn: 课堂里的数据展示

intro.en: Chart carries the Latin paper root charta- alongside its twin card.
intro.cn: chart 与孪生词 card 同携拉丁语「纸」词根 charta-。

latinIntro.en: The root charta also lives in charter and cartridge.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 charta 还存在于 charter 与 cartridge 中。

items.example: A chart is drawn on paper.
Write the new words on a card.
The chartist studied the price lines.
items.exampleCN: 图表分析者研究价格曲线。

items.meaning: a round chart cut into parts
items.example: Draw a pie chart of your day.
items.exampleCN: 画一张你一天的饼状图。

items.meaning: a chart with bars of different heights
items.example: The bar chart shows the votes.

items.meaning: a chart showing steps in order
items.example: Make a flow chart of the plan.

definition_zh: 记录；最高纪录；唱片；录制；档案
definition_en: a written or stored account; the best result achieved; a disc of music; to set down or capture for later use
core_image: 厚厚的登记簿上，一行行墨迹整齐排列
scene: 田径场上计时牌停在新的世界最好成绩，看台上掌声四起。 She broke the world record in the final race.
sceneCN: 这里 record 是「最高纪录」（第 2 个义项：已达成的最好成绩）；句意为她在决赛中打破了世界纪录。画面里可留意：停住的计时牌、看台上的掌声。

pos.zh: 记录；最高纪录；唱片；档案

derivatives.zh: 录音机；记录员
录音；录像
可录制的

senses.title: A stored account
senses.definition: a written or stored account of facts, events, or data
senses.definitionCN: 对事实、事件或数据的书面或电子留存
senses.example: The school keeps a record of every student.
senses.exampleCN: 学校保存着每名学生的记录。
senses.why: Recordari meant to bring something back to the heart, that is, to remember, and a record is memory made durable.
senses.whyCN: recordari 意为把某事重新放回心里，也就是记住，而记录就是被固定下来的记忆。

senses.title: The best result achieved
senses.definition: the best performance or result ever reached in a sport or activity
senses.definitionCN: 某项运动或活动中曾达到的最好成绩
senses.example: She broke the world record in the final race.
senses.exampleCN: 她在决赛中打破了世界纪录。
senses.why: A record once meant the line that holds the best result, and the word came to name the best result itself.
senses.whyCN: record 原指记载最好成绩的那一行，后来直接指最好成绩本身。

senses.title: A disc of music
senses.definition: a flat disc on which music or sound is stored
senses.definitionCN: 储存音乐或声音的扁平圆盘
senses.example: He still owns an old jazz record.
senses.exampleCN: 他还留着一张老爵士唱片。
senses.why: Music cut into a disc is a record in the physical sense, because the grooves store the sound.
senses.whyCN: 刻进圆盘的音乐是物理意义上的记录，因为沟槽储存着声音。

senses.title: To capture for later use
senses.definition: to store sound, images, or data so that they can be used later
senses.definitionCN: 把声音、图像或数据储存起来供以后使用
senses.example: They recorded the concert for the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为档案馆录制了这场音乐会。
senses.why: To record is to set something down for later recall, and a machine now performs that setting down.
senses.whyCN: 录制就是把某物记下以备日后回想，如今由机器来完成这一「记下」。

senses.title: An official file
senses.definition: the body of written evidence kept by a court, an office, or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 由法院、机关或机构保存的书面证据集合
senses.example: The court record shows two earlier warnings.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭档案显示此前有两次警告。
senses.why: An official file is a record kept by an institution, and the word widened from a single note to a body of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 官方档案是机构保存的记录，这个词从单条笔记扩展为一整套证据。

intro.en: Record begins at the heart: to remember is to bring a thing back to the heart, and to record is to fix that memory outside the body.
intro.cn: record 始于「心」：记住就是把事物放回心里，而记录则是把这份记忆固定在身体之外。

items.en: Cor, cordis meant heart, the seat of memory in older thought.
items.cn: cor、cordis 意为心，在更早的观念里是记忆所在之处。

items.en: Recordari meant to remember, literally to bring back to the heart.
items.cn: recordari 意为记住，字面就是「重新带回心里」。

items.en: Old French recorder carried both remembering and setting down in writing.
items.cn: 古法语 recorder 同时带有「记住」与「写下」的意思。

items.en: Middle English record named a witness, a written note, and the act of noting.
items.cn: 中古英语 record 指证人、书面笔录，以及记录的行为。

items.en: Modern English added the disc, the machine recording, and the sports best.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了唱片、机器录制与运动最高成绩。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same cord- core; the near-meaning group gathers words for stored information and discs.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 cord- 核心的词；近义组收表储存信息与唱片的词。

entries.definition: To tell a story in detail.
An agreement between parties.
Disagreement and conflict.
A written record of something.
An official list or record.
A regular written record of events.
A flat round object that stores sound.

normalIntro.en: The word is about memory kept outside the mind: a note, a disc, a file, a best score.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词讲的是存放在头脑之外的记忆：笔记、唱片、档案、最好成绩。

normal.en: Re plus cord: bring it back to the heart, and you remember; write it down, and you record.
normal.cn: re 加 cord：带回心里是记住，写下来就是记录。

normal.en: The noun stress is on the first syllable, the verb stress on the second.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Break a record means to do better than anyone before.
normal.cn: break a record 意为超过此前所有人。

normal.en: On record means officially written down and known.
normal.cn: on record 意为有正式记载。

normal.en: Record a song and keep a record use the same word in two directions.
normal.cn: record a song 与 keep a record 是同一个词的两种方向。

abstract.en: A record is a promise made to the future that this moment happened.
abstract.cn: 记录是对未来作出的承诺：这一刻确实发生过。

abstract.en: What a culture records is what it intends to remember.
abstract.cn: 一个文化记录什么，就是它打算记住什么。

abstract.en: Every record will fall; the keeping of it is what lasts longer.
abstract.cn: 每一项纪录都会被打败，而记录它的行为持续得更久。

examples.en: The school keeps a record of every student.
examples.cn: 学校保存着每名学生的记录。

examples.en: She broke the world record in the final race.
examples.cn: 她在决赛中打破了世界纪录。

examples.en: They recorded the concert for the archive.
examples.cn: 他们为档案馆录制了这场音乐会。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cord（心）：把事重新放回心里，就是记住；写下来留存，就是记录。

root: 拉丁 cor / cord-（心）→ recordari（回想，把事放回心里）→ 古法语 recorder → 中古英语 record → 英语 record；同族有 recorder、recording。

sensesIntro.en: The core is memory fixed outside the mind; the senses move from a written account to a best result, a disc, an act of capture, and an official file.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「固定在头脑之外的记忆」；义项从书面记录，到最好成绩、唱片、录制行为，再到官方档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick ledger filled with even lines of ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本厚厚的登记簿，一行行墨迹排列整齐。

branches.en: a ledger open on a desk
branches.cn: 桌上摊开的登记簿

branches.en: a scoreboard frozen at a new best
branches.cn: 停在最好成绩的计分牌

branches.en: a disc spinning on a turntable
branches.cn: 唱机上旋转的唱片

branches.en: a microphone capturing a concert
branches.cn: 捕捉音乐会的麦克风

branches.en: a file drawer marked official
branches.cn: 标着「官方」的档案抽屉

intro.en: The word joins the Latin word for heart to a prefix of return, and then spreads to discs, machines, and files.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语的「心」与表回返的前缀结合，再扩展到唱片、机器与档案。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin base is cor, heart, and recordari, to remember; the prefix re- carries the sense of return.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 cor（心）与 recordari（记住）；前缀 re- 带有「回返」之义。

definition_zh: 棒球运动；棒球；棒球用的（作定语）
definition_en: a game in which two teams hit a ball with a bat and run around four bases
core_image: 一只白色小球被木棒击中，飞过内野
scene: 放学后，学生们戴上帽子，在操场上分组挥棒打球。 Our class played baseball after school on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 baseball 是「棒球运动」（第 1 个义项：用棒击球并跑垒的比赛）；句意为星期五放学后我们班打了棒球。

derivatives.zh: 由 baseball 与 cap 组合而成，义为「棒球帽」
由 baseball 与 bat 组合而成，义为「棒球棒」
由 baseball 与 player 组合而成，义为「棒球运动员」

senses.title: The sport
senses.definition: a game in which two teams take turns hitting a ball with a bat and running around four bases
senses.definitionCN: 两队轮流用棒击球、绕四个垒奔跑的比赛
senses.example: Our class played baseball after school on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期五放学后我们班打了棒球。
senses.why: The compound joins base and ball, and the game is named after the two things a player uses most.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 base 与 ball 合在一起，比赛正是按球员最常用的两样东西命名。

senses.title: The ball
senses.definition: the small hard ball used in this game, with a stitched cover
senses.definitionCN: 这项运动使用的、表面有缝线的小硬球
senses.example: He hit the baseball over the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他把棒球击出了围栏。
senses.why: The second half of the compound keeps its literal meaning, so the object itself is also a baseball.
senses.whyCN: 复合词的后半保留了字面意思，所以那只球本身也叫 baseball。

senses.title: Of or for baseball
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean relating to or used in baseball
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词前，表示与棒球有关或供棒球使用
senses.example: He wore a blue baseball cap to the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一顶蓝色棒球帽去看比赛。
senses.why: Once the sport was well known, its name could stand in front of another noun as a label, like a badge.
senses.whyCN: 这项运动广为人知之后，它的名字就能放在另一名词前面作标签，像一枚徽章。

intro.en: Baseball is an English compound of base and ball, and the modern game took shape in the United States.
intro.cn: baseball 是 base 与 ball 的英语复合词，现代比赛形式在美国成形。

items.en: Greek basis meant a step or a pedestal, from the verb bainein, to go.
items.cn: 希腊语 basis 指台阶或基座，来自动词 bainein「走」。

items.en: Latin basis kept the sense of a base or foundation and passed through French into English as base.
items.cn: 拉丁语 basis 保留「基座、基础」之义，经法语以 base 进入英语。

items.en: Ball is the Germanic word for a round object, recorded in English from the Middle Ages.
items.cn: ball 是日耳曼语中表示圆形物的词，中古时期已见于英语。

items.en: The compound baseball is recorded in Britain in the eighteenth century, before the modern rules existed.
items.cn: baseball 这一复合词在十八世纪的英国已有记录，当时现代规则尚未形成。

items.en: The modern game with four bases and a bat spread in the United States in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 以四个垒和球棒为核心的现代比赛，在十九世纪的美国传播开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves of the compound and its common phrases; the near-meaning group gathers other bat-and-ball games and sports words.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两个成分及其常见搭配；近义组收其他用棒击球的运动和体育词。

entries.definition: One of the four points a player must reach in baseball, or the bottom part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垒；底部」，是 baseball 的前半部分。

entries.definition: The round object hit in the game; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「球」，是 baseball 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The wooden or metal club used to hit the ball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「棒球棒」，由 baseball 与 bat 组合而成。

entries.definition: A soft cap with a long front brim, worn in and out of the game.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「棒球帽」，帽檐较长，比赛内外都常戴。

entries.definition: A similar game played with a larger, softer ball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垒球」，规则相近，但用更大更软的球。

entries.definition: A bat-and-ball game popular in Britain and South Asia.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「板球」，是英国与南亚流行的击球运动。

entries.definition: An older British bat-and-ball game that resembles baseball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「圆场球」，是英国较早的击球运动，与棒球相似。

entries.definition: The general word for a game played for exercise or competition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运动」，是这类活动的总称。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real halves of the compound and the fixed phrases built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个复合词两个真实的组成部分，以及由它构成的固定搭配。

normal.en: Base plus ball: players run to bases and hit a ball, so the name lists the game's two essentials.
normal.cn: base 加 ball：球员跑垒、击球，名字正好列出比赛的两样核心。

normal.en: A baseball cap was first worn by players, then by everyone.
normal.cn: 棒球帽最初由球员佩戴，后来人人都戴。

normal.en: The ball in baseball is hard and small, unlike the bigger softball.
normal.cn: 棒球用的球又小又硬，与更大的垒球不同。

normal.en: A baseball field has four bases arranged in a diamond.
normal.cn: 棒球场有四个垒，排成菱形。

normal.en: Baseball came before basketball in English, and both names describe how the ball is used.
normal.cn: baseball 在英语中出现得比 basketball 早，两个名字都说明球的用法。

abstract.en: Picture a diamond of four white bags on the grass: a player must touch each one to score.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上四只白色垒包排成菱形：球员要逐个踩到才能得分。

abstract.en: The game is slow until the bat meets the ball, and then everyone moves at once.
abstract.cn: 比赛一直很慢，直到球棒击中球，所有人同时动起来。

abstract.en: One compound names a sport, a ball, and a hat, because a familiar word can label anything near it.
abstract.cn: 一个复合词可以指运动、球和帽子，因为熟悉的词能给身边任何东西贴标签。

examples.en: Our class played baseball after school on Friday.
examples.cn: 星期五放学后我们班打了棒球。

examples.en: He hit the baseball over the fence.
examples.cn: 他把棒球击出了围栏。

examples.en: She keeps her baseball cap in her school bag.
examples.cn: 她把棒球帽放在书包里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贝斯包」——背个包去打球，包里装着球和棒：棒球

root: baseball 是英语复合词，由 base（经法语来自拉丁语 basis，源头为希腊语 basis「台阶、基座」）与 ball（日耳曼语「圆形物」）组合而成。十八世纪已有记录，现代四垒制比赛在十九世纪的美国成形。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of baseball start from one compound: the sport itself, the hard ball used in it, and the attributive use that labels caps, bats, and fields.
sensesIntro.cn: baseball 的三个义项都从一个复合词出发：运动本身、比赛用的硬球，以及给帽子、球棒、球场贴标签的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white ball leaves the bat and rises over the infield grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白球离开球棒，飞过内野草地。

branches.en: THE GAME: base and ball together name the sport of running the bases after a hit.
branches.cn: 比赛线：base 与 ball 合起来，指击球后跑垒的这项运动。

branches.en: THE BALL: the second half keeps its literal sense, so the hard stitched ball is also a baseball.
branches.cn: 球线：后半保留字面义，所以带缝线的硬球也叫 baseball。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the sport's name moves in front of caps, bats, and fields as a modifier.
branches.cn: 标签线：运动的名字移到帽子、球棒、球场前面作定语。

branches.en: THE EQUIPMENT: the bat, the glove, and the ball are all named through the game.
branches.cn: 装备线：球棒、手套和球都借这项运动来命名。

branches.en: THE FIELD: four bases in a diamond shape organize the whole game.
branches.cn: 球场线：四个垒排成菱形，组织起整场比赛。

intro.en: Baseball is a two-part English compound, and its parts are still visible and usable on their own.
intro.cn: baseball 是两部分组成的英语复合词，两个成分至今仍能独立使用。

latinIntro.en: The base half goes back to Latin basis from Greek, while ball is Germanic; basis is the recorded Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 前半 base 可上溯到来自希腊语的拉丁语 basis，后半 ball 属日耳曼语；basis 是有记录的拉丁形式。

items.meaning: a bottom part, or one of four points in the game

items.example: The ball went over the fence.
Baseball is popular in many countries.
items.exampleCN: 棒球在许多国家很受欢迎。
它与 baseball 构成 baseball bat。
它与 baseball 构成 baseball cap。
它与 baseball 构成 baseball field。
它与 baseball 构成 baseball player。

items.example: It forms baseballs, meaning the balls.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 baseballs，指多个棒球。

definition_zh: 似乎；看起来像；看来
definition_en: to appear to be something or to appear to do something, or to make a statement less direct
core_image: 雾里一个模糊的人影，轮廓忽近忽远
scene: 雾里那个人影晃了一下，看着像熟人。 The figure seemed familiar in the fog.
sceneCN: 这里 seem 是「看起来像」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雾中的身影看起来很熟悉。

derivatives.zh: 表面上；看来
表面上的
不得体的

senses.title: Appear to be
senses.definition: to give the impression of being something
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，好像是某物
senses.example: The house seems very old.
senses.exampleCN: 这房子看起来很旧。
senses.why: This is the common linking use before an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这是接形容词时最常见的系动词用法。

senses.title: Appear to do
senses.definition: to give the impression of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 给人正在做某事的印象
senses.example: She seems to know the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她似乎知道答案。
senses.why: Seem can also introduce an action.
senses.whyCN: seem 也可以引出某个动作。

senses.title: Softening a statement
senses.definition: used to make a claim less direct or less certain
senses.definitionCN: 用于让陈述更委婉、更不确定
senses.example: It seems we have a problem.
senses.exampleCN: 看来我们遇到麻烦了。
senses.why: The word softens what follows it.
senses.whyCN: 该词使其后的说法变得委婉。

intro.en: Seem comes from Old Norse soema, to befit, from a root meaning fitting or suitable.
intro.cn: seem 源自古诺斯语 soema（适合），词根意为「相称、合适」。

items.en: Soema meant to befit or suit.
items.cn: soema 意为适合、相称。

items.en: The related adjective meant fitting.
items.cn: 相关形容词意为合适的。

items.en: English seem first meant to be fitting.
items.cn: 英语 seem 最初意为合适。

items.en: It shifted toward appear to be.
items.cn: 它逐渐转向「看起来是」的意思。

items.en: It now also softens statements politely.
items.cn: 如今它也用来礼貌地缓和陈述。

note.en: Seem is compared with similar-looking words and with other linking verbs.
note.cn: 把 seem 与形近词以及其他系动词作比较。

entries.definition: to notice with the eyes
the part of a plant that grows
to try to find
to look as if something is true
to have a certain appearance
to give a certain impression when heard

normalIntro.en: Seem means to look a certain way without proving it.
normalIntro.cn: seem 意为看起来如此，但并未证实。

normal.en: Seem is a linking verb like appear.
normal.cn: seem 和 appear 一样是系动词。

normal.en: It seems that means it appears that.
normal.cn: it seems that 意为「看起来……」。

normal.en: She seems tired means she looks tired.
normal.cn: she seems tired 意为她看起来很累。

normal.en: Seem to do describes an apparent action.
normal.cn: seem to do 描述一个看似发生的动作。

normal.en: Seemly and unseemly come from the same root.
normal.cn: seemly 与 unseemly 同出一源。

abstract.en: Seem lives in the gap between appearance and fact.
abstract.cn: seem 存在于外表与事实的缝隙里。

abstract.en: What seems true may only be partly true.
abstract.cn: 看似为真的，也许只是部分为真。

abstract.en: Every judgment begins with how things seem.
abstract.cn: 每个判断都始于事物呈现的样子。

examples.en: The house seems very old.
examples.cn: 这房子看起来很旧。

examples.en: She seems to know the answer.
examples.cn: 她似乎知道答案。

examples.en: It seems we have a problem.
examples.cn: 看来我们遇到麻烦了。

dict_mnemonic.text: seem 借自古诺斯语 soema（适合），由「相称」引申为「显得、似乎」，是常见的系动词。

root: 源自古诺斯语 soema（适合、相称），核心义「看上去相称、像是如此」。

sensesIntro.en: Seem means to appear to be, to appear to do, or to make a statement softer.
sensesIntro.cn: seem 意为似乎是、似乎做，或使陈述更委婉。

core.en: To present an appearance that may or may not be true.
core.cn: 呈现出可能真也可能不真的样子。

branches.en: Something gives a certain impression.
branches.cn: 某物给人某种印象。

branches.en: Someone looks as if doing something.
branches.cn: 某人看起来像是在做某事。

branches.en: A claim is made less direct.
branches.cn: 一个说法被说得更委婉。

branches.en: Both senses rest on appearance.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在外表之上。

branches.en: Politeness hides inside uncertainty.
branches.cn: 礼貌藏在不确定之中。

intro.en: Seem builds a small family around the idea of what is fitting.
intro.cn: seem 围绕「相称、得体」构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: This word came from Old Norse, so there are no Latin base forms to add.
latinIntro.cn: 该词来自古诺斯语，没有对应的拉丁语词根条目。

items.exampleCN: 她表面的平静掩盖着恐惧。

items.example: They argued in an unseemly way.
The unseemliness of the joke shocked her.
items.exampleCN: 这个笑话的粗俗让她震惊。

definition_zh: 四分之一；一刻钟；季度；城区；一节；住所
definition_en: one of four equal parts; fifteen minutes; a period of three months; a district of a city; one of the periods of a game; a place where someone lives
core_image: 一块圆饼被刀切成四等份，其中一份被叉子轻轻挑起
scene: 球场的计时牌跳进最后一格，观众站起来看表，教练把手里的战术板攥紧。 The home team scored twice in the final quarter of the game.
sceneCN: 这里 quarter 是「比赛的一节」（第 5 个义项：一场比赛被分成的四段之一）；句意为主队在比赛的最后一节两次得分。画面里可留意：计时牌、战术板、站起来的观众。

pos.zh: 四分之一；一刻钟；季度；城区；一节；住所

derivatives.zh: quarter 加 -ly，指每季度一次的，也可作副词与名词
quarter 与 final 复合，指四分之一决赛，即八进四的那一轮
head 与 quarters 复合，指总部所在之处，字面是「首要的营房」

senses.title: One of four equal parts
senses.definition: one of four equal parts into which a whole is divided
senses.definitionCN: 一个整体被分成四份时的其中一份
senses.example: A quarter of the class chose to walk to the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 班里四分之一的人选择走路去博物馆。
senses.why: Latin quartarius named a fourth part, and English kept the plain fraction sense at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quartarius 指第四份，英语把这个最朴素的分数义保留在词的核心。

senses.title: Fifteen minutes
senses.definition: one fourth of an hour, used especially in telling the time
senses.definitionCN: 一小时的四分之一，尤用于报时
senses.example: The train leaves at a quarter past six.
senses.exampleCN: 火车六点一刻出发。
senses.why: Since an hour divides neatly into four, the fourth part of an hour became the everyday name for fifteen minutes.
senses.whyCN: 既然一小时正好能分成四份，一小时的四分之一就成了十五分钟的日常说法。

senses.title: A period of three months
senses.definition: one of the four three-month periods into which a business or school year is divided
senses.definitionCN: 商业或学年被分成的四个三个月周期之一
senses.example: Sales rose sharply in the last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 销售额在最后一个季度大幅上升。
senses.why: A year is four quarters, so the fourth part of a year became the standard unit of business reporting.
senses.whyCN: 一年有四个季度，于是「一年的四分之一」成了商业报表的标准单位。

senses.title: A district of a city
senses.definition: an area of a city, especially one with its own character
senses.definitionCN: 城市中一片区域，尤指有自身特色的区域
senses.example: The old quarter is full of narrow lanes and small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区满是狭窄的巷子和小店铺。
senses.why: Old French quartier meant a fourth part of a town as well as a lodging, and the place sense survived in English.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 quartier 既指城镇的四分之一区，也指住处，这层「地方」的意思在英语里保留了下来。

senses.title: One of the periods of a game
senses.titleCN: 一节；一局中的四分之一
senses.definition: one of the four periods into which some sports divide their playing time
senses.definitionCN: 某些运动把比赛时间分成的四段之一
senses.example: He scored twice in the final quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一节两次得分。
senses.why: Sports that divide play into four equal periods simply call each period a quarter.
senses.whyCN: 把比赛分成四个等长时段的运动项目，就直接把每一段叫作 quarter。

senses.title: A place to live
senses.definition: a place where soldiers or staff live, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 士兵或员工的住处，通常用复数
senses.example: The crew returned to their quarters after the drill.
senses.exampleCN: 演习结束后，船员们回到自己的住处。
senses.why: To quarter troops meant to lodge them in a district, and the plural quarters came to mean the lodgings themselves.
senses.whyCN: to quarter troops 本指把军队安排到某片区域驻扎，复数 quarters 由此转指住处本身。

intro.en: Quarter comes from the Latin word for a fourth part, formed from the ordinal fourth and carried into English through French.
intro.cn: quarter 源自拉丁语表示「第四份」的词，由序数词「第四」构成，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quartus was the ordinal fourth, the root of a whole family of words about dividing something into four.
items.cn: quartus 是序数词「第四」，是一整族关于把事物四等分的词的根。

items.en: Quartarius named a fourth part, whether of a measure, of a day or of a town.
items.cn: quartarius 指第四份，无论是度量、一天还是一座城镇的第四份。

items.en: Old French quartier meant both a fourth part and a district or lodging place.
items.cn: 古法语 quartier 既指第四份，也指一片城区或住处。

items.en: Middle English quarter took the fraction sense and added the senses of time and place.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quarter 接受了分数义，又增加了时间与地点两层意思。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for fractions, for fifteen minutes, for business periods, for city areas and for sports periods.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指分数、十五分钟、商业周期、城区与比赛时段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of fourth; the near-meaning group gathers words for fractions, districts and set periods.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「第四」词干上的词；近义组收表示分数、城区与固定时段的词。

entries.definition: A unit of liquid measure equal to two pints.
entries.definitionCN: 等于两品脱的液量单位。

entries.definition: Happening once every three months.
The round before the semifinals in a knockout competition.
entries.definitionCN: 淘汰赛中半决赛之前的一轮。

entries.definition: A group of four musicians or a piece for four.
entries.definitionCN: 四位乐手组成的团体或为四人写的乐曲。

entries.definition: The ordinal number matching one of four equal parts.
entries.definitionCN: 与四等份之一相应的序数词。

entries.definition: An area of a town or country with a clear boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇或国家中有明确边界的一片区域。

entries.definition: A fixed period of time in a school or business year.
entries.definitionCN: 学年或商业年度中一段固定的时间。

entries.definition: A length of time with a defined start and end.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确起止的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with the fourth part of a whole and spreads outward to the fourth part of an hour, of a year, of a town and of a game.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从整体的第四份出发，向外扩展到一小时、一年、一座城与一场比赛的第四份。

normal.en: Quarter and quartet both begin from four, one naming a part and the other naming a group of four.
normal.cn: quarter 与 quartet 都从「四」出发，一个指一份，一个指四人的组合。

normal.en: A quarter past the hour is fifteen minutes after it, and a quarter to is fifteen minutes before.
normal.cn: a quarter past 是整点后十五分钟，a quarter to 是整点前十五分钟。

normal.en: Business reports arrive four times a year, so each report covers one quarter.
normal.cn: 商业报表一年来四次，所以每份报表覆盖一个季度。

normal.en: Living quarters keeps the old military sense of lodgings in the plural.
normal.cn: living quarters 以复数保留了旧时军中「营房、住处」的意思。

normal.en: Basketball and American football divide their games into four quarters, each with its own clock.
normal.cn: 篮球和美式橄榄球把比赛分成四节，每一节都有自己的计时。

abstract.en: Dividing a whole into four is the simplest way to make a big thing feel manageable.
abstract.cn: 把一个整体分成四份，是让庞然大物变得可控的最简单办法。

abstract.en: Every quarter of a city has its own memory, which is why the word for a fraction also names a place.
abstract.cn: 城市的每一片街区都有自己的记忆，所以表示分数的词也能指一个地方。

abstract.en: A quarter of an hour is short, yet whole decisions are often made inside it.
abstract.cn: 一刻钟很短，但许多决定往往就在这一刻钟里做成。

examples.en: Only a quarter of the students passed the first test.
examples.cn: 只有四分之一的学生通过了第一次测验。

examples.en: We meet at a quarter to eight every Monday.
examples.cn: 我们每周一七点三刻见面。

examples.en: The company moved its headquarters to the old quarter of the city.
examples.cn: 公司把总部搬到了这座城市的旧城区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔特」——把一张大饼阔气地切成四块，其中一块就是 quarter，四分之一。

root: 拉丁语 quartus（第四）→ quartarius（第四份）→ 古法语 quartier → 英语 quarter；同族有 quartet、quarterly、quarterfinal。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fourth part; the senses apply that fourth part to an hour, a year, a town, a game and a set of lodgings.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「第四份」；义项把这份四分之一分别用到一小时、一年、一座城、一场比赛以及一处住处上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round flatbread cut cleanly into four, one piece lifted by a fork.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张圆饼被利落地切成四块，其中一块被叉子挑起。

branches.en: a knife crossing a round loaf twice
branches.cn: 一把刀在圆面包上横竖各切一下

branches.en: a clock face split at fifteen-minute marks
branches.cn: 表盘上按十五分钟分出的刻度

branches.en: a report filed four times a year
branches.cn: 一年上交四次的报表

branches.en: a narrow lane behind an old shop
branches.cn: 老店铺后面的一条窄巷

branches.en: a whistle ending a period and a door closing on a barracks
branches.cn: 结束一节的哨声与营房关上的门

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin ordinal for fourth, a noun of portion, the French form and English endings that create time and place words.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语序数「第四」、表示份额的名词、法语形式，以及构成时间与地点词的英语词缀搭建起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around quartus is short and regular.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 quartus 的拉丁词群短而规整。

core_image: 纸上写着一行完整的字，末尾落下一个句点

senses.title: Group of words
senses.definition: a group of words that expresses a complete thought
senses.definitionCN: 表达完整思想的一组词
senses.example: He wrote a very long sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他写了一个很长的句子。
senses.why: This is the grammar sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是语法义。

senses.title: Court punishment
senses.definition: a punishment ordered by a court
senses.definitionCN: 法庭判处的惩罚
senses.example: The judge gave him a light sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官给了他轻判。
senses.why: A court's judgment is also called a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的判断也叫 sentence。

senses.title: To order punishment
senses.definition: to order a punishment in court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上判处惩罚
senses.example: The court sentenced him to two years.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判处他两年徒刑。
senses.why: The noun becomes the judge's action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为法官的动作。

intro.en: Sentence comes from Latin sententia, an opinion or judgment, from sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: sentence 出自拉丁语 sententia（意见、判断），源于 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or think.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或思考。

items.en: Sententia meant an opinion or judgment.
items.cn: sententia 意为意见或判断。

items.en: Old French sentence kept the judgment sense.
items.cn: 古法语 sentence 保留了判断义。

items.en: English sentence meant opinion or legal judgment.
items.cn: 英语 sentence 意为意见或法律判决。

items.en: The grammar sense became dominant.
items.cn: 语法义后来占据主导。

note.en: Sentence is compared with similar-looking words and with grammar and law words.
note.cn: 把 sentence 与形近词以及语法、法律类词作比较。

relating to a sentence
the ability to feel
a small group of words
a part of a sentence with a verb
a court's decision

normalIntro.en: Sentence is a complete thought in words, and also a court's judgment.
normalIntro.cn: sentence 是用词语表达的完整思想，也是法庭的判决。

normal.en: A sentence begins with a capital letter.
normal.cn: 句子以大写字母开头。

normal.en: A topic sentence states the main idea.
normal.cn: 主题句陈述主要观点。

normal.en: A life sentence lasts many years.
normal.cn: 终身监禁持续很多年。

normal.en: The judge passed sentence at noon.
normal.cn: 法官中午宣判。

normal.en: Sentence and sentiment share a root.
normal.cn: sentence 与 sentiment 同根。

abstract.en: A sentence closes a thought the way a door closes a room.
abstract.cn: 句子结束一个思想，就像门关上一个房间。

abstract.en: Judgment and grammar both put things in order.
abstract.cn: 判决与语法都在给事物排定秩序。

abstract.en: The same word can hold a thought or a punishment.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能装思想，也能装惩罚。

examples.en: He wrote a very long sentence.
examples.cn: 他写了一个很长的句子。

examples.en: The judge gave him a light sentence.
examples.cn: 法官给了他轻判。

examples.en: The court sentenced him to two years.
examples.cn: 法庭判处他两年徒刑。

dict_mnemonic.text: sentence 出自拉丁语 sententia（意见、判断），源于 sentire（感觉、思考），本义「所想的判断」，后兼指语法句子与法庭判决。

root: 源自拉丁语 sententia（判断、意见），出自 sentire（感觉、思考），核心义「完整表达出的判断」。

sensesIntro.en: Sentence means a complete group of words, a court's punishment, or to order that punishment.
sensesIntro.cn: sentence 意为完整的句子、法庭判决或宣判。

core.en: A complete judgment, in words or in law.
core.cn: 用言语或法律作出的完整判断。

branches.en: Words closing into one complete idea.
branches.cn: 收束成一个完整思想的词语。

branches.en: A punishment declared by a court.
branches.cn: 法庭宣布的惩罚。

branches.en: The act of declaring that punishment.
branches.cn: 宣布该惩罚的行为。

branches.en: Grammar and law both close a matter.
branches.cn: 语法与法律都在了结一件事。

branches.en: The ruling and the saying of it share a name.
branches.cn: 判决与宣判共用一个名称。

intro.en: Sentence belongs to the Latin sentire family of feeling and judging.
intro.cn: sentence 属于拉丁语 sentire（感觉、判断）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sententia and sentire are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sententia 与 sentire 是历史词根。

items.meaning: a complete word group or judgment

items.meaning: the act of giving a sentence

items.exampleCN: 他说教式的语气让他们厌烦。

definition_zh: 主要的；首要的；最初的；初级的；原生的；（美国）初选
definition_en: first in importance, order, or development; basic rather than derived
core_image: 一排门中最先打开的那一扇，所有人从这里进入
scene: 急救现场，医生先检查呼吸、出血与意识。 Her primary check covered breathing, bleeding and awareness, and everything else waited until those three were answered.
sceneCN: 这里 primary 是「首要的、第一位的」（第 1 个义项：在重要性上排第一）；句意：她的首要检查覆盖呼吸、出血和意识，其余项目都等这三项有答案之后才做。图中可辨识物件：急救包、担架、监护仪、手电筒、评估表；对应第 1 个义项。
