senses.title: First in importance
senses.definition: more important than all others
senses.definitionCN: 比其余一切更重要
senses.example: Safety is our primary concern.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是我们的首要关切。
senses.why: Latin primarius means 'of the first rank'. The word ranks things: one item is placed in the first position, and the others are measured against it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 primarius 意为“第一等的”。这个词给事物排名：一项被放到第一位，其余都以它为参照。

senses.title: First in order or time
senses.definition: coming first in a sequence or process
senses.definitionCN: 在序列或过程中最先出现
senses.example: The primary stage of the reaction takes seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 反应的初始阶段只需几秒。
senses.why: Order and importance borrow the same image. What comes first in time is often what must be dealt with first, so sequence slides into priority.
senses.whyCN: 次序与重要性借用同一意象。时间上最先的，往往也是必须先处理的，于是序列滑向优先。

senses.title: Basic or elementary
senses.definition: of the first level of education or skill
senses.definitionCN: 教育或技能的第一层
senses.example: Children learn to read in primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在小学学习阅读。
senses.why: Primary education is the first tier, before secondary. The word names a floor of a building rather than a value judgment.
senses.whyCN: 初等教育是第二级之前的第一层。这个词命名建筑的一层楼，而非价值判断。

senses.title: Chief or main
senses.definition: the main or principal part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的主要或主体部分
senses.example: The primary cause was a failed valve.
senses.exampleCN: 主要原因是阀门失效。
senses.why: Here primary is close to principal: it picks out the leading element in an explanation. The two words share a root but differ in role.
senses.whyCN: 这里 primary 接近 principal：它挑出解释中的主导要素。两词共享词根，但角色不同。

senses.title: Original, not derived
senses.definition: of a source or record, created at the time, not based on another
senses.definitionCN: 来源或记录在当时产生，而非依据他物
senses.example: Historians prefer primary sources such as letters.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家偏爱书信这类原始资料。
senses.why: Research divides evidence into first-hand and second-hand. A primary source is the earliest layer; everything else is commentary on it.
senses.whyCN: 研究把证据分为第一手与第二手。原始资料是最早的一层，其余都是对它的评论。

senses.title: A US primary election
senses.definition: a state election in which voters choose party candidates
senses.definitionCN: 选民在其中选出政党候选人的州级选举
senses.example: She won the New Hampshire primary.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢下了新罕布什尔州初选。
senses.why: American politics uses the noun for the first screening election in a campaign. The word keeps its 'first stage' sense: the primary precedes the general election.
senses.whyCN: 美国政治用这个名词指竞选中的第一场筛选性选举。它保留“第一阶段”义：初选在普选之前。

senses.title: A primary feather
senses.definition: one of the flight feathers on the outer part of a bird's wing
senses.definitionCN: 鸟翼外侧的飞行羽毛
senses.example: The hawk's primaries spread wide in flight.
senses.exampleCN: 猎鹰飞行时初级飞羽大张。
senses.why: Ornithology numbers feathers from the leading edge outward. The primaries are the first flight feathers, so the word's ordinal sense becomes anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 鸟类学从翼前缘向外编号。初级飞羽是最先的飞行羽毛，于是序数义变成解剖名。

senses.title: First in a chemical chain
senses.definition: of a carbon atom or compound, attached to one other carbon group
senses.definitionCN: 碳原子或化合物只与一个其他碳基相连
senses.example: Primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes.
senses.exampleCN: 伯醇氧化成醛。
senses.why: Chemistry labels structures by position in a chain: primary, secondary, tertiary. The naming is ordinal, borrowed straight from the Latin 'first rank'.
senses.whyCN: 化学按链上的位置标记结构：伯、仲、叔。命名是序数性的，直接借自拉丁语“第一等”。

senses.title: One of the primary colors
senses.definition: in color theory, a color from which others can be mixed
senses.definitionCN: 色彩理论中可混合出其他颜色的基色
senses.example: Red, blue, and yellow are primary colors in painting.
senses.exampleCN: 在绘画中，红、蓝、黄是三原色。
senses.why: Color theory treats some hues as underived: they cannot be produced by mixing the others. Primary here means 'not made from anything else', the root sense of primus.
senses.whyCN: 色彩理论把某些色相视为不可再分：它们不能由其他颜色混合产生。这里 primary 意为“不是由别物制成”，是 primus 的根本义。

intro.en: Primary comes straight from Latin primarius, 'of the first rank', built on primus 'first'. English uses it for rank, for sequence, for schooling, and for anything that is not derived from something else.
intro.cn: primary 直接来自拉丁语 primarius“第一等的”，建立在 primus“第一”之上。英语用它表等级、次序、学校教育，以及任何不是由他物派生的事物。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'first in order, original, principal'.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“次序第一、原始的、主要的”。

items.en: From Latin primarius 'of the first rank or quality', from primus 'first'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 primarius“第一等或第一品质的”，源出 primus“第一”。

items.en: primus is traced to PIE *per- 'before, first', also behind prime, prior, and prince. The reconstruction is standard.
items.cn: primus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”，也见于 prime、prior、prince。该重构是通行说法。

items.en: The educational sense 'elementary' and the logical sense 'original, not derived' become established.
items.cn: 教育义“初级的”与逻辑义“原始的、非派生的”确立。

items.en: The noun primary for a direct nominating election appears in American politics.
items.cn: 名词 primary 指直接提名选举，出现在美国政治中。

items.en: Modern English spreads the word across medicine, chemistry, biology, and color theory, always keeping the ordinal core.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词铺到医学、化学、生物学与色彩理论，始终保留序数核心。

note.en: The first group shares the primus stem; the second is about adjectives that also mean chief or first.
note.cn: 第一组共享 primus 词干，第二组看同样表示“首要”或“第一”的形容词。

entries.definition: mainly; chiefly. It is primary plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地；首要地。它是 primary 加 -ly。

entries.definition: the state of being first in rank. It comes from Latin primatus.
entries.definitionCN: 首位；优先。来自拉丁语 primatus。

entries.definition: first in rank or quality; also a peak state. It shares primus directly.
entries.definitionCN: 第一等的；鼎盛状态。它直接共享 primus。

entries.definition: first in importance. It is close to primary sense 1 but is not used for stages or schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 重要性第一的。它接近 primary 第 1 义，但不用于阶段或教育。

entries.definition: at the very beginning. It marks sequence only, not rank.
entries.definitionCN: 在最开始的。它只标记次序，不标记等级。

entries.definition: of the simplest level. It matches the schooling sense but not the 'chief' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 最简层次的。它对应教育义，不对应“首要”义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin primus 'first', the primarius rank word, the primary/principal pair, and the primary source idea.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 primus“第一”、primarius 的等级义、primary 与 principal 这对词，以及“原始资料”概念。

normal.en: Primus means 'first'. Everything primary is first in some line: rank, time, school, or origin.
normal.cn: primus 意为“第一”。一切 primary 都在某条线上第一：等级、时间、学校或起源。

normal.en: Primary vs principal: both mean chief, but only primary is used for stages, schools, and sources.
normal.cn: primary 与 principal：两者都指首要，但只有 primary 用于阶段、学校与资料。

normal.en: Primary source is first-hand evidence; secondary source is commentary on it.
normal.cn: 原始资料是第一手证据；二手资料是对它的评论。

normal.en: Primary school is the first tier of schooling, not a school that is 'more important' than others.
normal.cn: 小学是教育的第一层，不是“比别的学校更重要”的学校。

normal.en: In chemistry, primary, secondary, and tertiary are positions on a carbon chain, numbered from the end.
normal.cn: 化学中，伯、仲、叔是碳链上的位置，从末端编号。

abstract.en: Priority is a spatial metaphor: we place one thing at the front of a line and call it first.
abstract.cn: 优先是一种空间隐喻：我们把一件事放到队伍最前，称它为第一。

abstract.en: The first is not always the best: primary means earliest, and earliest often means simplest.
abstract.cn: 最先的未必最好：primary 意为最早，而最早往往意味着最简单。

abstract.en: A primary source is powerful because it has not yet been interpreted; it is the world before commentary.
abstract.cn: 原始资料之所以有力，是因为它尚未被解释；它是评论之前的世界。

examples.en: Public safety is the primary goal of the policy.
examples.cn: 公共安全是这项政策的首要目标。

examples.en: The study relies on primary sources from the period.
examples.cn: 这项研究依赖该时期的一手资料。

examples.en: He won the primary by a narrow margin.
examples.cn: 他以微弱优势赢得初选。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来马瑞”——扑过来的马群里，第一匹最显眼 → primary 首要的、第一的

root: 拉丁语 primarius“第一等的”，源出 primus“第一”；更早为原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”。同族有 prime、prior、prince。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of primary, all ordinal: first in rank, in time, in school, in evidence, in a chemical chain, or in a color system. The word always places something at the head of a line.
sensesIntro.cn: primary 的九个义项都是序数性的：在等级、时间、学校、证据、化学链或颜色系统中排第一。这个词总是把某物放在一条线的头部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first position at the head of a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线最前端的第一位置。

branches.en: RANK: the most important item is placed first and the rest measured against it.
branches.cn: 等级：最重要的项被放在第一，其余以它为参照。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: the first stage in time, including the first election of a campaign.
branches.cn: 次序：时间上的第一阶段，包括竞选的第一场选举。

branches.en: SCHOOL: the first tier of education, basic rather than advanced.
branches.cn: 学校：教育的第一层，基础而非高级。

branches.en: ORIGIN: first-hand evidence and underived colors are not made from anything else.
branches.cn: 起源：第一手证据与不可再分的原色不是由他物制成。

branches.en: ANATOMY AND CHEMISTRY: the ordinal sense becomes naming for leading feathers and chain positions.
branches.cn: 解剖与化学：序数义变成对前缘飞羽与链上位置的命名。

intro.en: Primary is an adjective and a noun. English adds -ly and -cy, and the primus root also gives prime, primer, and prince.
intro.cn: primary 既是形容词也是名词。英语加 -ly 与 -cy，primus 词根还生成 prime、primer、prince。

latinIntro.en: Latin primarius 'of the first rank' and primus 'first' sit beside primatus 'first place' and principium 'beginning'. The family is about ordinal priority.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primarius“第一等”与 primus“第一”旁边是 primatus“首位”与 principium“开端”。这个词族关乎序数优先。

items.meaning: the state of being first in rank or importance
first in rank; the best years; a prime number
items.meaningCN: 第一等的；鼎盛期；质数（同源词）

items.meaning: a royal ruler; a leading figure
chief; a school head; a sum of money
items.meaningCN: 主要的；校长；本金（同源，义不同）

definition_zh: 回忆起；召回；撤销；记忆力
definition_en: to remember something from the past; to order a person or product back; to cancel officially; the power to remember
core_image: 一只手指向身后，把远处的画面拉回眼前
scene: 老人翻开旧相册，指着一张褪色的照片停住。 She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 recall 是「回忆起」（第 1 个义项：把过去的记忆唤回）；句意为她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。画面里可留意：翻开的相册、褪色的照片。

derivatives.zh: 可召回的；可回忆的
回忆；召回
未被召回的

senses.title: To remember
senses.definition: to bring a past event or detail back into the mind
senses.definitionCN: 把过去的事件或细节重新带回心里
senses.example: She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。
senses.why: Re- means back, and call means to summon, so the word pictures a memory being called back to the present.
senses.whyCN: re- 意为「回」，call 意为「召唤」，因此这个词描绘记忆被唤回当下。

senses.title: To call back
senses.definition: to order a person or a product to return
senses.definitionCN: 命令某个人或某件产品返回
senses.example: The company recalled thousands of faulty toys.
senses.exampleCN: 公司召回了数千件有缺陷的玩具。
senses.why: The literal image of calling someone back became an official order to return, first for envoys and later for goods.
senses.whyCN: 把某人唤回的字面形象，变成了正式的返回命令，先是针对使节，后来针对商品。

senses.title: To cancel officially
senses.definition: to withdraw a decision, an offer, or a law by official action
senses.definitionCN: 以官方行动撤回决定、提议或法律
senses.example: The council recalled the unpopular rule.
senses.exampleCN: 议会撤销了那条不受欢迎的规定。
senses.why: A cancelled decision is sent back to those who made it, and the image of calling back covers that reversal.
senses.whyCN: 被撤销的决定被送回做出决定的人那里，而「唤回」的形象正涵盖这种反转。

senses.title: The power to remember
senses.definition: the ability to remember things, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 记住事物的能力，作名词使用
senses.example: His recall of names is remarkably quick.
senses.exampleCN: 他记名字的速度快得惊人。
senses.why: When the act of calling back is viewed as a capacity, the verb turns into a noun naming memory itself.
senses.whyCN: 当「唤回」这一行为被视为一种能力时，动词就转为指称记忆本身的名词。

intro.en: Recall is a native calling verb with a Latin prefix: to call back is first a voice, then a memory, then an order.
intro.cn: recall 是本族的「呼喊」动词加拉丁前缀：唤回先是声音，再是记忆，最后是命令。

items.en: Ceallian meant to call out, the native verb behind call.
items.cn: ceallian 意为呼喊，是 call 背后的本族动词。

items.en: Norse kalla, to call, reinforced the same verb in northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kalla（呼喊）在英格兰北部强化了同一个动词。

items.en: The Latin prefix re-, meaning back, joined call to make recall.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 意为「回」，与 call 结合成 recall。

items.en: Middle English recallen meant both to call back and to remember.
items.cn: 中古英语 recallen 既指唤回，也指记起。

items.en: Modern English extended recall to products, officials, and the noun for memory.
items.cn: 现代英语把 recall 扩展到产品、官员，以及表记忆的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs with a similar opening; the near-meaning group gathers words for remembering and for summoning back.
note.cn: 形近组收开头相似的动词；近义组收表记忆与唤回的词。

entries.definition: To move back suddenly.
To withdraw a public statement.
To register as a member.
To keep or bring back in mind.
To gather memories back with effort.
To get something back.
To order someone to come.

normalIntro.en: The word is call plus back: a voice calls, and what was distant returns.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 call 加「回」：声音一唤，远处的东西就回来。

normal.en: Re plus call: to call back a face, a product, or a rule.
normal.cn: re 加 call：把面孔、产品或规定唤回来。

normal.en: Recall a memory is the everyday sense; product recall is the official one.
normal.cn: recall a memory 是日常义；product recall 是官方义。

normal.en: The noun has the same spelling, so recall can name the power to remember.
normal.cn: 名词拼写相同，因此 recall 也能指记忆力。

normal.en: Beyond recall means so far gone that it cannot be called back.
normal.cn: beyond recall 意为久远到再也唤不回来。

normal.en: Keep the double l: recall, recalled, recalling.
normal.cn: 注意双写 l：recall、recalled、recalling。

abstract.en: Memory is a call across time, and the past answers only if it still lives in us.
abstract.cn: 记忆是穿越时间的一次呼唤，过去只有在仍活在我们心里时才会应答。

abstract.en: A recall of a product is an admission that something once sold should not have been.
abstract.cn: 召回产品，就是承认某件已售出之物本不该售出。

abstract.en: What a society chooses to recall is what it chooses to be.
abstract.cn: 一个社会选择记住什么，就是选择成为什么。

examples.en: She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
examples.cn: 她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。

examples.en: The company recalled thousands of faulty toys.
examples.cn: 公司召回了数千件有缺陷的玩具。

examples.en: His recall of names is remarkably quick.
examples.cn: 他记名字的速度快得惊人。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 call（呼唤）：把记忆唤回来就是回忆；把人或产品唤回来就是召回。

root: 古英语 ceallian / 古诺斯语 kalla（呼喊）+ 前缀 re-（回）→ 中古英语 recallen → 现代英语 recall；同族有 recalling、recallable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is calling something back; the senses move from memory to products, to cancelled decisions, and to memory as a power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西唤回」；义项从记忆，到产品，到被撤销的决定，最后到作为一种能力的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pointing backwards, pulling a distant scene into view.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指向身后，把远处的画面拉回眼前。

branches.en: a face rising from an old photograph
branches.cn: 一张脸从旧照片里浮起

branches.en: toys pulled from shop shelves
branches.cn: 玩具从货架上被收回

branches.en: a rule struck from the book
branches.cn: 一条规定被从册子上划去

branches.en: a quick list of names in the mind
branches.cn: 脑中飞快列出的一串名字

branches.en: a memory called back and a decision called back
branches.cn: 唤回记忆，也撤回决定

intro.en: A native English verb of calling takes a Latin prefix, and the resulting word spreads from voices to memories and to official orders.
intro.cn: 英语本族的「呼喊」动词接上拉丁前缀，所得之词从声音扩展到记忆与官方命令。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is the prefix re-, meaning back; the verb call is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁元素是前缀 re-，意为「回」；动词 call 是英语本族词。

definition_zh: 垃圾箱；储物箱；扔掉（口语）
definition_en: a container for waste or for storing things
core_image: 一个方正的塑料箱，盖子半开，里面装着要丢掉的东西
scene: 厨房角落的垃圾箱已经满了，妈妈让孩子把它拿出去倒掉。 Please put the paper in the bin.
sceneCN: 这里 bin 是「垃圾箱」（第 1 个义项：装废弃物的容器）；句意为请把纸放进垃圾箱。

forms.label: 过去式与过去分词（动词）

derivatives.zh: 由 dust 与 bin 组合而成，义为「垃圾桶」
由 bin 与 man 组合而成，义为「垃圾清运工」，英式用法

senses.title: A container for waste
senses.definition: a container into which rubbish is thrown
senses.definitionCN: 用来扔废弃物的容器
senses.example: Please put the paper in the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 请把纸放进垃圾箱。
senses.why: Old English bin named a box or a receptacle, often for grain; when waste became a daily matter, the same word attached to the box that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bin 指箱、槽，多用来装谷物；当垃圾成为日常事务后，同一个词就附到了装垃圾的箱子上。

senses.title: A storage box
senses.definition: a large container used for storing goods, such as grain, fruit, or coal
senses.definitionCN: 用来存放货物的大箱子，如装谷物、水果或煤的箱子
senses.example: The apples are stored in a wooden bin.
senses.exampleCN: 苹果存放在一个木箱里。
senses.why: Storage is the oldest job of the bin, so this sense simply keeps the original use of the word alive.
senses.whyCN: 储物是 bin 最古老的用途，所以这个义项只是让这个词最初的用法活下来。

senses.title: To throw something away
senses.definition: to throw something away, used in informal British speech
senses.definitionCN: 把某物丢掉，用于非正式的英式口语
senses.example: He binned the old magazines.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧杂志扔掉了。
senses.why: The verb is the noun in action: putting something into the waste bin, which in speech simply means discarding it.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词在行动：把东西放进垃圾箱，在口语里就简化成「丢掉」。

intro.en: Bin is an old English word for a box, and its link to a Latin basket word is suggested but not certain.
intro.cn: bin 是英语里古老的「箱子」用词，它与拉丁语「篮子」一词的关系有人提出，但不确定。

items.en: Old English bin named a box or a receptacle, especially one for grain or stores.
items.cn: 古英语 bin 指箱子或容器，尤其是装谷物与货物的那种。

items.en: A similar Latin word benna meant a basket, and the two may be related, though this is not certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语中有一个相似的词 benna 表示篮子，二者可能有关，但并不确定。

items.en: The word stayed in use for storage containers of many kinds through the Middle English period.
items.cn: 在中古英语时期，这个词一直用于各种储物容器。

items.en: As rubbish became a daily concern, the container for it took the same name and bin became the usual word for a waste box.
items.cn: 随着垃圾成为日常问题，装垃圾的容器也用了同一个名字，bin 于是成为「垃圾箱」的常用词。

items.en: Today bin covers waste bins, storage bins, and even the act of throwing something away in speech.
items.cn: 今天 bin 可指垃圾箱、储物箱，口语里甚至可指「扔掉」这个动作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short rhyming or similar words; the near-meaning group collects other containers and waste words.
note.cn: 形近组收押韵或读音相近的短词；近义组收其他容器与垃圾用词。

entries.definition: To tie or fasten something; it begins like bin but has a long vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捆绑」，开头与 bin 相同，但元音更长。

entries.definition: A seed used as food; it looks similar in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「豆」，拼写与 bin 相近。

entries.definition: A small round bread roll.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小圆面包」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: The plural of bin, with a voiced ending.
entries.definitionCN: bin 的复数形式，词尾读作浊音。

entries.definition: A container made of woven material, often for carrying things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮子」，多用编织材料制成，常用来提东西。

entries.definition: Any object used to hold something, the general word for a bin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「容器」，是 bin 的上位泛指词。

entries.definition: The American word for a waste bin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾桶」，是美式说法。

entries.definition: A very large metal container for waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大型垃圾箱」，指很大的金属垃圾容器。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded old sense, the real compounds, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的古老义项、真实复合词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English bin meant a storage box, and that sense still lives in a wooden bin for apples.
normal.cn: 古英语 bin 指储物箱，这个义项至今活在装苹果的木箱里。

normal.en: Latin benna meant a basket, and the link to bin is possible but not certain.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 benna 指篮子，它与 bin 的联系有可能，但并不确定。

normal.en: Dustbin and binman keep the waste sense, and bin liner names the bag inside.
normal.cn: dustbin 与 binman 保留「垃圾」义，bin liner 则指套在里面的袋子。

normal.en: In British speech, to bin something is simply to throw it away.
normal.cn: 在英式口语里，to bin something 就是「把它扔掉」。

normal.en: Spell b-i-n: three letters, with a short vowel between two consonants.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-n，三个字母，两个辅音之间夹一个短元音。

abstract.en: See a square plastic box with the lid half open and paper inside: that is bin.
abstract.cn: 想象一个方形塑料箱，盖子半开，里面装着纸，那就是 bin。

abstract.en: Fill the same box with apples instead of paper and the waste sense becomes storage.
abstract.cn: 把同一个箱子装满苹果而不是纸，垃圾义就变回储物义。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the square box bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那个方箱子把意思带回来。

examples.en: Please put the paper in the bin.
examples.cn: 请把纸放进垃圾箱。

examples.en: The apples are stored in a wooden bin.
examples.cn: 苹果存放在一个木箱里。

examples.en: He binned the old magazines.
examples.cn: 他把旧杂志扔掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「冰」——冰块扔进垃圾箱就化了：垃圾箱

root: bin 来自古英语 bin，指箱子或容器，尤其用于装谷物与货物。拉丁语中有一个相似的词 benna 表示篮子，二者可能相关，但不确定。随着垃圾成为日常事务，装垃圾的容器也用了这个词，bin 遂成为「垃圾箱」的常用说法；口语里还可作动词，表示「扔掉」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of bin are one box seen three ways: a box for waste, a box for storage, and the act of putting something into it.
sensesIntro.cn: bin 的三个义项是同一个箱子被看作三种样子：装垃圾的箱、装货物的箱，以及把东西放进去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square plastic box with the lid half open
core.cn: 核心意象：一个盖子半开的方形塑料箱

branches.en: THE WASTE: the box for rubbish is the commonest modern sense.
branches.cn: 垃圾线：装废弃物的箱子是今天最常见的义项。

branches.en: THE STORAGE: the oldest use keeps the box for grain, fruit and goods.
branches.cn: 储物线：最古老的用法保留着装谷物、水果与货物的大箱。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the noun turned verb means putting something into that box.
branches.cn: 动作线：名词转动词，指把东西放进那个箱子。

branches.en: THE SAME BOX: waste and storage are two jobs of one container.
branches.cn: 同一个箱：垃圾与储物是同一个容器的两种用途。

branches.en: THE SHORT STEP: naming the box and naming the act are only one step apart.
branches.cn: 一步之差：给箱子命名和给动作命名只差一步。

intro.en: Bin is a base noun, so the items below are its inflections and the compounds built on it.
intro.cn: bin 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的屈折形式以及由它构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin benna, a basket, is a possible relative but not a proven source, so it is listed with that caution.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 benna 指篮子，可能是远亲而非确证的来源，因此按此谨慎列出。

items.meaning: more than one, or he does
items.meaningCN: 表示复数或第三人称单数

items.meaning: a bag that lines a container

definition_zh: 精确地；确切地；恰好；正是；完全正确
definition_en: in a precise way; quite so; used to agree strongly
core_image: 天平砝码完美归零：指针停在正中央
scene: 实验室里滴管停在刻度线上，老师点头认可。 The recipe calls for exactly two hundred grams of flour.
sceneCN: 这里 exactly 是「精确地」（第 1 个义项：不多不少）；句意是食谱要求精确两百克面粉。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀的基础形容词，义为「精确的；确切的」
由 exact 加 -ness 构成，义为「精确；准确」
由 exact 加 -ing 构成，义为「严苛的；要求高的」

senses.title: In a precise way
senses.definition: in a way that is completely correct, with no mistake or difference
senses.definitionCN: 完全正确的方式，毫无差错或偏差
senses.example: Please follow the instructions exactly.
senses.exampleCN: 请严格按说明操作。
senses.why: The Latin root means driven out or measured out, so the image is weighing to the final grain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「称量完毕、耗尽」，画面是称量到最后一粒。

senses.title: Just so, precisely that
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is completely right or true
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事完全正确或属实
senses.example: That is exactly what I wanted to say.
senses.exampleCN: 那正是我想说的话。
senses.why: The needle rests in the middle: the statement and the truth balance perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 指针停在正中：陈述与事实完全平衡。

senses.title: An agreement marker
senses.definition: a spoken reply meaning you agree completely
senses.definitionCN: 口语应答，表示完全同意
senses.example: Exactly! That is the whole point of the story.
senses.exampleCN: 完全正确！这正是故事的全部要点。
senses.why: From weighing exactness grows a quick word for a perfect match of minds.
senses.whyCN: 由称量的精确生长出对思想完全契合的快速应答。

intro.en: Exactly comes from exact, from Latin exagere, to weigh out or drive out. The modern word keeps the picture of a perfectly finished measurement.
intro.cn: exactly 由 exact 派生，exact 来自拉丁语 exagere「称量完、耗尽」。现代词保留称量完美的画面。

items.en: Latin exigere meant to drive out, to weigh out, or to complete a measurement.
items.cn: 拉丁语 exigere 意为驱出、称量完毕或完成测量。

items.en: Exactus, its past participle, meant measured out completely, with nothing left over.
items.cn: 过去分词 exactus 意为称量完毕、分毫不差。

items.en: English borrowed exact in the fifteenth century as a rare scholarly word.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 exact，原为罕见学术词。

items.en: In the scientific age exact became a prized word for precise measurement.
items.cn: 科学时代 exact 成为精确测量的珍贵词汇。

items.en: Exactly grew into agreement talk: exactly so, exactly right.
items.cn: exactly 生长出应答用法：exactly so、exactly right。

note.en: The first group collects the exact family; the second collects near meanings about precision and agreement.
note.cn: 第一组收集 exact 词族；第二组收集与「精确、赞同」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: precise and correct in every detail
entries.definitionCN: 精确的。去掉 -ly 的基础形容词。

entries.definition: making strict demands, hard to satisfy
entries.definitionCN: 严苛的。由 exact 加 -ing 构成，词义已偏移。

entries.definition: to pull out or remove; shares the ex- out-prefix
entries.definitionCN: 提取；拔出。同享 ex-「向外」前缀。

entries.definition: in a precise way, a close synonym
entries.definitionCN: 精确地；正是。最接近的同义词。

entries.definition: completely yes, an agreeing reply
entries.definitionCN: 绝对地；完全正确。应答语。

entries.definition: exactly at a point, as in just six o'clock
entries.definitionCN: 恰好；刚刚。表示时点恰好。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the weighing root and classroom talk.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于称量词根与课堂用语的具体联想。

normal.en: ex- means out and the root means weighed out: nothing is left to chance.
normal.cn: ex-（出）+ 词根（称量完）：分毫不差。

normal.en: Exactly the same is the phrase every comparison needs.
normal.cn: exactly the same 完全一样，比较题常用。

normal.en: Exactly! is the quickest word of strong agreement.
normal.cn: Exactly! 赞同时的口头禅，一句顶十句。

normal.en: Not exactly softens a polite disagreement.
normal.cn: not exactly 不完全是，礼貌否定好帮手。

normal.cn: 谐音：「一脚扎克踢」——一脚踢中靶心，帮助拼读，不是词源。

examples.en: Copy the poem exactly as it is written.
examples.cn: 一字不差地抄写这首诗。

examples.en: The train left at exactly half past seven.

examples.en: Exactly! You have found the answer.
examples.cn: 完全正确！你找到答案了。

sensesIntro.en: Exactly weighs to the last grain: precise action, perfect match, and a spoken yes.
sensesIntro.cn: exactly 称量到最后一粒：精确行动、完全契合，以及口头的「完全正确」。

intro.cn: exactly 在 exact 词根上显示拉丁 ex- 前缀；词族小而精确。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere 'weigh out, drive out' is the shared ancestor of this family.

definition_zh: 有害的；造成伤害的
definition_en: causing or likely to cause harm or damage
core_image: 玻璃碴混进米饭：吃下去就会割伤身体的东西
scene: 工厂把污水排进小河，下游的鱼越来越少，村民都明白这水有毒。 The factory dumped dirty water into the river, which was harmful to the fish.
sceneCN: 这里 harmful 是「有害的」（第 1 个义项：对健康或生命造成损害）；脏水毒害鱼群，harmful 直接描述这种造成伤害的性质。

derivatives.zh: 伤害；损害，harmful 的基础名词，指实际的伤害
有害地，由 harmful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
无害的，由 harm 加后缀 -less 构成，表示没有伤害

senses.title: Causing damage to health or life
senses.definition: causing physical injury or damage to health
senses.definitionCN: 造成身体伤害或损害健康
senses.example: Smoking is harmful to your lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟对你的肺有害。
senses.why: Harm means injury, and adding the suffix -ful turns a noun of injury into an adjective of cause: something full of harm.
senses.whyCN: harm 意为伤害，加后缀 -ful 把「伤害」名词变成「充满伤害」的形容词，于是指造成伤害的事物。

senses.title: Damaging in effect or influence
senses.definition: having a bad effect on a situation, person, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对局面、人或事物产生坏影响
senses.example: Spreading rumors is harmful to team trust.
senses.exampleCN: 散布谣言对团队信任有害。
senses.why: Injury is not only physical; the image of cutting and breaking extends to trust, reputation, and relationships.
senses.whyCN: 伤害不限于身体，「割裂、破坏」的意象延伸到信任、名声与关系，harmful 由此覆盖抽象损害。

intro.en: Harmful is built from the old word harm plus the adjective suffix -ful.
intro.cn: harmful 由古词 harm 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成。

items.en: Old English hearm meant injury, evil, or pain, and was already a common word in poetry and law.
items.cn: 古英语 hearm 意为「伤害、恶、痛苦」，在诗歌与法律文本中已很常用。

items.en: It goes back to a Germanic root meaning to shame or injure, shared with Old Saxon harm and Old High German harm.
items.cn: 它可追溯到日耳曼词根，意为「羞辱、伤害」，与古撒克逊语 harm 等同源。

items.en: In Middle English, harm was both noun and verb, and the compound harm-doing described injury in action.
items.cn: 中古英语中 harm 兼作名词与动词，复合词 harm-doing 描述正在进行的伤害。

items.en: The suffix -ful, from Old English full, turned nouns into adjectives meaning full of.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 来自古英语 full，把名词变成「充满……的」形容词。

items.en: Modern English fixed harmful as the standard adjective for things that cause damage to health or nature.
items.cn: 现代英语把 harmful 固定为描述损害健康或自然的事物标准形容词。

note.en: Words shaped like or close in meaning to harmful.
note.cn: 与 harmful 形近或义近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 伤害；损害，同根基础名词

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word harmful.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 harmful 的五个锚点。

normal.en: harm + -ful
normal.cn: 结构「harm + -ful」：充满伤害，即有害。

normal.en: harmful to health
normal.cn: 搭配「harmful to health」（有害健康）是最常见用法。

normal.en: harmful vs harmless
normal.cn: 对比例「harmful vs harmless」（有害 vs 无害），后缀决定方向。

normal.en: harmful effects
normal.cn: 短语「harmful effects」（有害影响）把抽象义固定下来。

normal.en: harm as the core
normal.cn: 先记 harm（伤害），再记 harmful（有害的），顺序自然。

abstract.en: See glass shards mixed into rice: eating means getting cut.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃碴混进米饭：吃下去就会被割伤——这就是 harmful 的画面。

abstract.en: Feel smoke filling a clean room and making people cough.
abstract.cn: 感受烟雾充满洁净房间、让人咳嗽：有害之物正在充满环境。

abstract.en: Extend the cut from skin to trust.
abstract.cn: 把「割伤」从皮肤延伸到信任：谣言也是 harmful。

examples.en: Doctors say too much salt is harmful to the heart.
examples.cn: 医生说过多的盐对心脏有害。

examples.en: The harmful gases from the factory made the nearby trees die.
examples.cn: 工厂排出的有害气体让附近的树木枯死了。

examples.en: Reading in dim light is less harmful than people think.
examples.cn: 在昏暗光线下看书并不像人们想的那么有害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈姆服」——吃了变质的火腿，「哈姆」让你难受，因为它是 harmful（有害的）。

root: harmful 由 harm（伤害，古英语 hearm，源自日耳曼词根「羞辱、伤害」）加形容词后缀 -ful（充满）构成，字面即「充满伤害的」。同族词还有 harmlessly、harmlessness 等。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from bodily injury to damage in abstract fields.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从身体伤害延伸到抽象领域的损害。

core.cn: 核心意象：藏在食物里的玻璃碴

branches.cn: 损害健康与身体的事物

branches.en: Influences that erode trust or value
branches.cn: 侵蚀信任或价值的影响

branches.en: One root image: cutting and breaking
branches.cn: 同一根意象：割裂与破坏

branches.en: Chemicals and gases that poison
branches.cn: 有毒的化学品与气体

branches.en: Rumors and habits that corrode
branches.cn: 腐蚀关系的谣言与习惯

intro.cn: harmful 展示了 harm 加后缀的高能产英语构词模式。

latinIntro.cn: harm 为日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 邻居；邻人；邻近的人或物；毗邻
definition_en: a person who lives next door or close by; a person or thing standing beside another; and, as a verb, to be next to a place
core_image: 两家院墙之间只隔一道矮篱，篱上晾着同一根绳子上的衣物
scene: 楼道里的纸箱还没拆完，对门的人先端来一壶热水。 The neighbour across the hall brought a kettle of hot water before the boxes were even opened.
sceneCN: 这里 neighbour 是「邻居」（第 1 个义项：住在近旁的人）；句意为纸箱还没打开，对门那位就端来一壶热水。图中可辨识物件：楼道、纸箱、水壶。

derivatives.zh: 由 neighbour 加 -ing 构成，义为「邻近的；相邻的」
由 neighbour 加 -ly 构成，义为「邻里般的；友善的」
由 neighbourly 加 -ness 构成，义为「邻里情谊；友善」
neighbourhood 的美式拼写，义为「街区；邻里」

senses.title: A person who lives close by
senses.definition: someone who lives next door or very near to one's home
senses.definitionCN: 住在隔壁或离家很近的人
senses.example: Our neighbour upstairs plays the piano every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。
senses.why: The Old English compound joins neah, near, with gebur, a dweller, so the word names the person who dwells near you rather than a friend or a relative.
senses.whyCN: 古英语复合词把 neah（近）与 gebur（居住者）拼在一起，字面上指的就是「住得近的人」，与朋友或亲戚无关。

senses.title: A person or thing placed beside another
senses.definition: the person sitting or standing beside you, or a thing lying next to another of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 坐在或站在你旁边的人，或与其他同类相邻的事物
senses.example: She leaned towards her neighbour at the table to hear the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她凑向同桌的邻座，想听清祝酒词。
senses.why: Because the word marks only position, it can be used for a stranger in the next seat, and the same logic lets it describe a country lying beside another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只标记位置，所以能用来指旁边座位上的陌生人，同样的逻辑也让它可以形容一个挨着另一个的国家。

senses.title: To stand next to a place
senses.definition: to be situated immediately beside or near a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 位于某处紧邻的位置
senses.example: The small farm neighbours a protected stretch of river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。
senses.why: Having named the dweller nearby, English turns the word into a verb for the dwelling itself standing beside another, which is a short step from a person to a place.
senses.whyCN: 既然已经指「住在近旁的人」，英语就把这个词改成动词，指房屋本身紧挨着另一处；从人到地点只差一小步。

intro.en: Neighbour is an Old English compound of two plain words, one meaning near and one meaning dweller. The British spelling keeps ou, and American English writes neighbor.
intro.cn: neighbour 是古英语里两个很朴素的词拼成的，一个表示「近」，一个表示「居住者」。英式拼写保留 ou，美式写作 neighbor。

items.en: The first element goes back to a reconstructed Germanic root for near, the same source as near and the archaic nigh.
items.cn: 第一个成分可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「近」的重构词根，与 near、古旧的 nigh 同源。

items.en: Neah meant near or close, and it survives as the first half of the compound neahgebur.
items.cn: neah 意为近、靠近，作为复合词 neahgebur 的前半保留下来。

items.en: Gebur meant a dweller or a fellow worker of the land, so neahgebur was the person living close by.
items.cn: gebur 指居住者或一同种地的人，所以 neahgebur 就是住得不远的人。

items.en: Middle English reshaped the word as neighebor, and the vowel and spelling shifted several times before settling.
items.cn: 中古英语把它改写成 neighebor，元音和拼写来回变过几次才固定下来。

items.en: Modern British English keeps neighbour with ou, while American English simplifies it to neighbor; the meaning and the history are the same.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留带 ou 的 neighbour，美式简化为 neighbor；两者的含义与来历完全相同。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the near element or merely the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who live in a place.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「近」这一成分的词，以及只是读音相近的词；近义组收表示住在某处的人。

entries.definition: Close in space or time, the idea that also sits inside the first half of neighbour.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上接近的；neighbour 的前半也藏着这个「近」的想法。

entries.definition: An older word for near, now mostly literary or dialectal.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「近」的较古老词，现多用于文学或方言。

entries.definition: The long loud cry of a horse; it only looks and sounds like neighbour, and its root is imitative.
entries.definitionCN: 马的长嘶声；只是与 neighbour 形音相近，词源是拟声，二者无关。

entries.definition: A person who lives in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 住在某个地方的人；居民。

entries.definition: A person who lives in a particular house or area, often used in compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 住在某处房屋或地区的人，常用于复合词。

entries.definition: A person who lives in the area being talked about.
entries.definitionCN: 住在所谈地区的人；本地人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of near and dweller, and the British spelling keeps an ou that American English drops.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「近」与「居住者」复合而成，英式拼写保留一个美式会去掉的 ou。

normal.en: Neah means near and gebur means dweller, so a neighbour is simply the dweller nearest to you.
normal.cn: neah 意为近，gebur 意为居住者，所以邻居就是离你最近的居住者。

normal.en: The -bour part is the old word for a dweller, not the English word for a harbour, so do not read it as a port.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 -bour 是古语「居住者」，不是英语里表示港口的词，别把它读成码头。

normal.en: The verb use follows the noun, since a farm can neighbour a river: the word only marks what stands close.
normal.cn: 动词用法跟着名词走，农场可以 neighbour 一条河，因为这个词只标记「紧挨着」的位置。

normal.en: American English writes neighbor, and the shorter form follows the same pattern as harbor and color.
normal.cn: 美式写作 neighbor，缩短的拼写与 harbor、color 遵循同一规律。

normal.en: Next-door neighbour is the fixed phrase for the person in the house beside yours.
normal.cn: next-door neighbour 是固定说法，指紧挨着你家的那户人。

abstract.en: A word built from near and dweller turns geography into a relationship: closeness itself becomes a kind of company.
abstract.cn: 一个由「近」和「居住者」拼成的词，把地理变成关系：距离近本身就成了一种陪伴。

abstract.en: The British ou and the American missing u are the same word wearing two passports.
abstract.cn: 英式多写一个 u、美式省掉它，是同一个词拿着两本护照。

abstract.en: Calling a country a neighbour borrows the warmth of a doorstep for something as cold as a border.
abstract.cn: 把一个国家叫作 neighbour，是把门槛边的暖意借给了边界这样冰冷的东西。

examples.en: Our neighbour upstairs plays the piano every evening.
examples.cn: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。

examples.en: She turned to her neighbour at the table and smiled.
examples.cn: 她转向同桌的邻座，笑了一下。

examples.en: The farm neighbours a stretch of protected river.
examples.cn: 这座农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内个伯」——巷子里那位伯伯就住在隔壁，张嘴一喊就是他；记住 neighbour 是邻居。

root: 古英语 neah（近）加 gebur（居住者）复合为 neahgebur，中古英语作 neighebor，现代英式拼写 neighbour，美式拼写 neighbor。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who dwells near; from that, the meaning widens to anyone or anything beside you and then becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「住得不远的人」；由此词义扩到身边任何人或物，最后又变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low hedge between two yards, with washing hung across it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两家院子之间一道矮篱，篱上晾着同一根绳子上的衣物。

branches.en: a kettle handed over a shared doorstep
branches.cn: 从共用的门槛递过来的一壶水

branches.en: two families hanging washing on one line
branches.cn: 两家人把衣服晾在同一根绳上

branches.en: a stranger in the next seat on a long flight
branches.cn: 长途航班上邻座的陌生人

branches.en: a farm fence running beside a river
branches.cn: 沿着河边伸长的农场篱笆

branches.en: a border stone that two gardens share
branches.cn: 两个花园共用的一块界石

intro.en: The word is a compound of an old adjective for near and a noun for dweller, and English later added endings that make it an adjective and a noun of quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「近」的古形容词与表示「居住者」的名词复合而成，英语后来又加上词尾，使它成为形容词和表示情谊的名词。

latinIntro.en: This word is Germanic in origin and has no reliable Latin cognate; its parts and its family are Old English and English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它的构件和词族都属于古英语和英语。

definition_zh: 活着的；有活力的；仍然存在的；充满……的
definition_en: living and not dead, or full of energy, or still in use, or full of something
core_image: 清早的操场上有人跑步呼吸
scene: 清晨的操场上，几个人在跑步，呼吸有力。 The old tree is still alive.
sceneCN: 这里 alive 是「活着的」（第 1 个义项：仍有生命）；句意为这棵老树仍然活着。

pos.zh: 形容词：活着的；有活力的；仍然存在的

derivatives.zh: 生命
生活；居住
活泼的

senses.title: Living, not dead
senses.definition: having life and not being dead
senses.definitionCN: 拥有生命而不是死亡
senses.example: The fish was still alive.
senses.exampleCN: 那条鱼仍然活着。
senses.why: The old phrase on life meant being in life, so alive first says that life is still there.
senses.whyCN: 古短语 on life 意为处在生命之中，所以 alive 首先表示生命仍在。

senses.title: Full of energy
senses.definition: showing quick energy and interest
senses.definitionCN: 表现出充沛的精力与兴趣
senses.example: The class came alive after the game.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏之后全班活跃起来。
senses.why: A living body moves and reacts, so being alive also pictures energy in action.
senses.whyCN: 活着的身体会动会反应，所以 alive 也画出行动中的活力。

senses.title: Still existing
senses.definition: kept in use or in memory
senses.definitionCN: 仍被使用或仍被记住
senses.example: The old custom is still alive.
senses.exampleCN: 这个旧习俗仍然存在。
senses.why: A custom that has not died out is pictured as still having life.
senses.whyCN: 没有消失的习俗被画成「仍然有生命」。

senses.title: Full of living things
senses.definition: full of moving things, used in alive with
senses.definitionCN: 满是活动的东西，用于 alive with
senses.example: The pond was alive with fish.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘里满是鱼。
senses.why: A place crowded with moving creatures looks as if life fills it.
senses.whyCN: 一个充满游动生物的地方，看起来就像被生命填满。

intro.en: The recorded history of alive is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 alive 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old phrase on life meant in life or with life.
items.cn: 古短语 on life 意为在生命之中。

definition_zh: 跟随；接着；遵循；听懂；关注
definition_en: to go or come after someone or something; to act according to; to understand; to watch with interest
core_image: 沿着前面那人的脚印一直走下去
scene: 林间小路上，孩子们一个牵着一个排成一列往前走。 Follow me and do not look back.
sceneCN: 这里 follow 是动词「跟随」（第 1 个义项：走在某人后面、循其路线）；句意为跟着我，不要回头看。

derivatives.zh: 由 follow 加名词后缀构成，义为「追随者；粉丝」
由 follow 加动名词后缀构成，义为「下列的；接着的」
由 follow 加 up 构成，义为「后续；跟进」
社交平台上关注他人的人，义为「关注者」

senses.title: To go after someone
senses.definition: to go or come after a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 走在一个或物之后
senses.example: The dog follows its owner everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 狗到处跟着主人。
senses.why: The core image is walking on the same track behind another.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是沿同一轨迹走在他人身后。

senses.title: To act according to rules or advice
senses.definition: to obey rules, or to act as advised
senses.definitionCN: 按规则行事或照建议行动
senses.example: Drivers must follow the traffic rules.
senses.exampleCN: 司机必须遵守交通规则。
senses.why: Rules walk ahead of us like guides, so obeying them is following.
senses.whyCN: 规则像向导走在前面，服从它们就是跟随。

senses.title: To happen after in time
senses.definition: to happen after something else in time or order
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或顺序上接在别的事之后
senses.example: Dinner followed the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会后用了晚餐。
senses.why: One event walking behind another in time mirrors people on a path.
senses.whyCN: 时间上一前一后的事件，正如路上前后而行的人。

senses.title: To understand what is said
senses.definition: to understand spoken words or a story
senses.definitionCN: 听明白话语或故事
senses.example: Do you follow what I mean?
senses.exampleCN: 你听懂我的意思了吗？
senses.why: Keeping pace with an argument is keeping pace with a speaker.
senses.whyCN: 跟上论证的节奏，就是跟上说话人的脚步。

senses.title: To watch with interest
senses.definition: to pay close attention to news, sport, or social media accounts
senses.definitionCN: 密切留意新闻、体育或社交账号
senses.example: Millions follow this star online.
senses.exampleCN: 数百万人网上关注这位明星。
senses.why: Eyes, like feet, can trail a person day after day.
senses.whyCN: 目光如脚步，可以日复一日追着一个人。

senses.title: The rear of the body
senses.definition: the part of the body from the neck down to the hips on the rear side
senses.definitionCN: 身体后侧从颈到臀的部分
senses.example: He carried the bag on his back.
senses.exampleCN: 他把书包背在背上。
senses.why: The old word named this ridge, so the rear of the body is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古词指这道脊背，所以身体后部就是第一义。

senses.title: The rear side of a thing
senses.definition: the side of something that is opposite to its front
senses.definitionCN: 某物与正面相对的那一面
senses.example: The garden is at the back of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 花园在房子的后面。
senses.why: The body's rear side is borrowed for any object, which gives the sense of the rear part.
senses.whyCN: 身体的后侧被借到任何物体上，于是有「后部」的义项。

senses.title: To an earlier place
senses.definition: to or toward a place where one was before
senses.definitionCN: 回到或朝以前所在的地方
senses.example: She came back after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 她午饭后回来了。
senses.why: Moving toward the side behind you is moving toward where you came from, which gives the sense of return.
senses.whyCN: 朝身后的那一面移动，就是朝来处移动，于是有「回来」。

senses.title: To support
senses.definition: to give help or approval to a person or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 给人或计划以帮助或赞同
senses.example: The whole class backed the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 全班都支持这个计划。
senses.why: Standing at a person's back is standing behind him, which turns the noun into the verb of support.
senses.whyCN: 站在一个人的背后就是为他撑腰，于是名词变成表示支持的动词。

senses.title: A person of no party
senses.definition: a politician or voter not belonging to a party
senses.definitionCN: 不属于任何党派的政治人物或选民
senses.example: An independent won the seat this time.
senses.exampleCN: 这次一位无党派人士赢得了席位。
senses.why: No flag, only the person's own name.
senses.whyCN: 不举旗，只署本人的名字。

intro.en: Independent is depend with in- (not) and -ent. The Latin root pendere means to hang; to be independent is not to hang from anyone.
intro.cn: independent 由 depend 加否定前缀 in- 与形容词后缀 -ent 构成。拉丁词根 pendere 意为悬挂；independent 即不挂在任何人身上。

items.en: Latin pendere meant to hang; payments once hung from the giver.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂；付账本像挂在付钱人身上。

items.en: de- plus pendere formed dependere: to hang down, then to rely.
items.cn: de- 加 pendere 构成 dependere：垂挂，引申为依赖。

items.en: Medieval Latin dependentem described one who hangs on another.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 dependentem 描述依附他人者。

items.en: Old French dependant passed the word on.
items.cn: 古法语 dependant 继续传承该词。

items.en: Middle English added in- to make independent, not hanging.
items.cn: 中古英语加上 in-，构成 independent「不悬挂的」。

items.en: Modern English extended it from people to nations and studies.
items.cn: 现代英语把它从人扩展到国家与研究。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the hang-root family. The meaning group compares words for standing alone.
note.cn: 形近组收录「悬挂」词根词族；词义组比较表示独自站立的词。

entries.definition: the noun of the same family.

a hanging swinging weight.

having its own control.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the hanging root, the voter use and the be independent of pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「悬挂」词根、无党派用法与 be independent of 句式。

normal.en: in- means not; dependent means hanging: not hanging.
normal.cn: in- 表否定，dependent 表悬挂：不悬挂。

normal.en: be independent of is the fixed pattern.
normal.cn: be independent of 是固定句式。

normal.en: An independent voter belongs to no party.
normal.cn: 无党派选民不属于任何党派。

normal.en: pendulum and suspend share the swinging-hang root.
normal.cn: pendulum 与 suspend 共享悬挂摆动的词根。

normal.en: dependent is the twin still hanging on.
normal.cn: dependent 是还挂着的孪生词。

abstract.en: One image: a rider letting go of the handlebars.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：骑车人松开扶手。

abstract.en: Independent is your own flag with your own name.
abstract.cn: independent 是只署自己名字的旗。

abstract.en: Two clocks that never touch still keep true time.
abstract.cn: 互不相触的两只钟照样走准时间。

examples.en: The country has been independent since nineteen sixty.
examples.cn: 该国自一九六零年起独立。

examples.en: She is an independent woman with her own business.
examples.cn: 她是拥有自己事业的独立女性。

examples.en: The findings were confirmed by independent researchers.
examples.cn: 研究结果得到独立研究者的证实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因迪潘登特」：不用「等」人「攀登」，自己登顶， independent。

root: 拉丁语 de-「向下」+ pendere「悬挂」→ dependere「垂挂、依赖」→ 拉丁/古法语 dependent「依附的」→ 加否定前缀 in- 得 independent「不依赖的」。

sensesIntro.en: Independent is the loosened hand: free nations, free decisions, self-fed wallets, unlinked studies, and voters under no flag.
sensesIntro.cn: independent 是松开的手：自由国家、自己做主、自食其力、互不牵连的研究，以及不举旗的选民。

core.en: Standing without hanging: nothing above pulls or feeds you.
core.cn: 不悬挂地站立：没有东西在上面牵引或喂养你。

branches.en: NATIONHOOD: an independent nation.
branches.cn: 国家层面：独立的国家。

branches.en: DECISION: old enough to be independent.
branches.cn: 决定：到了能自主的年纪。

branches.en: SUPPORT: independent of his parents.
branches.cn: 供养：不再依赖父母。

branches.en: UNLINKED: independent conclusions.
branches.cn: 互不牵连：互不影响的结论。

branches.en: NEUTRALITY: an independent won the seat.
branches.cn: 中立：无党派者赢得席位。

intro.en: Independent builds independently, independence and the opposite dependent.
intro.cn: independent 构成 independently、independence 及反义词 dependent。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the hanging verb behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示整个词族背后的悬挂动词。

items.example: An independent judge heard the case.
items.exampleCN: 一位独立法官审理此案。
